docs.title: How to Connect Bing Webmaster Tools to Perplexity with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Bing holds a second set of numbers about the same site, and almost nobody reads it. Impressions and clicks sit on one screen, the queries that produced them on another, crawl behaviour on a third, and inbound links somewhere else. Connecting Bing Webmaster Tools to Perplexity through CorpusIQ MCP turns those screens into one question, answered with the site and the window attached.

The comparison is the point. A page that ranks on Google and not on Bing usually has a technical cause, not a content one, and the two consoles never put the numbers side by side.
tags: connect Bing Webmaster Tools to Perplexity

docs.title: Why Connect Bing Webmaster Tools to Perplexity?
docs.text:
• Volume. "How many impressions and clicks did the site get from Bing last month?"
  • Query quality. "Which queries bring impressions with an average position worse than 10?"
  • Index state. "Is /pricing in the Bing index, and when was it last crawled?"
  • Crawl health. "How many pages did Bing crawl last week, and did any return an error?"
  • Links. "Which pages carry the most inbound links?"
  • Read-only by capability. The retrieval tools documented on this page return Bing Webmaster data to the assistant. They do not submit sitemaps, change verification or alter crawl settings.
tags: connect Bing Webmaster Tools to Perplexity

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Bing Webmaster Tools to CorpusIQ. Sign in with the Microsoft account that holds the verified sites. The connector lists every site that account has verified.
  2. Add CorpusIQ to Perplexity as a custom remote MCP server, using the endpoint from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. Ask a site question. CorpusIQ picks the verified site URL the question refers to, then reads traffic, queries, crawl statistics or a single URL as the question requires.
  4. Perplexity answers with the site and the date window named, so the figure can be reproduced in the console.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs keep query text, per-user tool-call metadata and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
tags: connect Bing Webmaster Tools to Perplexity

docs.text:

In Perplexity

  1. Open Settings and find the MCP servers section.
  2. Add a custom MCP server and paste the endpoint:
https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp

Then ask something the console can answer, for example how many clicks the site earned from Bing last month. Call the site list first when the account holds several properties, so the question lands on the right one.

docs.text: Which sites can I connect?  Every site the authorised Microsoft account has verified in Bing Webmaster Tools. A site that is not verified under that account does not appear.  Can Perplexity submit a sitemap or change a setting?  No. The retrieval tools documented on this page read data. Sitemap submission, verification and crawl settings stay in the console.  Does it read one page or the whole site?  Both. docs.title: How to Connect CallRail to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Calls are the part of marketing that spreadsheets miss. A form fill lands in a CRM with a campaign attached. A phone call lands in a call tracker with a tracking number, a duration and a source, and the story stops there unless somebody joins it back to the campaign by hand. Connecting CallRail to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP makes the call record queryable. You authorize read-only access once, ask which campaigns produced calls and how those calls went, and get an answer with the account, the window and the source attached.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only and does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational query logs are retained for up to 30 days.

docs.title: What Questions Can You Ask?
docs.text:
• "How many calls came in last month, and how long did they last on average?"
  • "Which tracking numbers received the most calls this quarter?"
  • "Which source sent the most calls, and did that change week over week?"
  • "Which companies under this account are generating calls and which are quiet?"
  • "Show me the calls from the campaign I spent the most on."
  • "Do the calls arrive at the same time as the ad clicks, or later?"

The last question is the one that changes budgets. Call timing against spend timing tells you whether the phone is an impulse channel or a considered one.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What does the connector expose?  Five read actions: the accounts the connection can reach, a single account summary with its features, the companies (tracked businesses) under an account, the tracking numbers configured under an account, and the calls themselves with tracking number, duration, start time, source and caller data. Every read after the account list is scoped to one account, so the first call is always the account lookup.  Is this read-only?  Yes. The connector lists accounts, companies, trackers and calls. It does not create, tag, edit or delete anything in CallRail. Write access is not exposed at all, not merely hidden behind a confirmation step.  Does it return transcripts, form submissions or lead scores?  No. The call record is what it returns: who called, on which tracking number, from which source, when, and for how long. Anything CallRail computes beyond that record, such as transcription, form capture or scoring, is not part of this connector's payload. Ask for what the record holds rather than assuming the rest is available.  How do I get true call attribution?  Join the call record to the ad or analytics record. The tracking number and the call source are the join keys, so with [Google Ads](connect-google-ads-to-chatgpt.md) or [Google Analytics](connect-google-analytics-to-chatgpt.md) connected on the same MCP server, "which campaign drove calls, and which of those calls lasted over two minutes" is one question across two connectors. Attribution you can defend means showing the join, not asserting the conclusion.  Does it work across several accounts or several clients?  Each CorpusIQ user authorizes their own CallRail access, and the account list read returns every account that connection can reach. An agency can hold several clients under one authorization and ask per-account questions without reconnecting. Revoking the connection in CallRail ends the connector's reach immediately.  What should I check before trusting a call number?  Check the window and the account, then check the tracking numbers. A call that arrived on a shared or untracked number carries the wrong source, and a report that silently mixes numbers will look complete while being wrong. The connector returns the tracking number for exactly this reason: it lets the answer be audited.  Where is my data stored?  It is not. Retrieval happens on demand against the live CallRail API. CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational query logs may persist for up to 30 days. See our [security documentation](../security/) for the detail.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. You sign in to CorpusIQ and connect CallRail.
  2. CallRail shows its consent screen. You approve read access for the account.
  3. You add the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. See the Quick Start guide.
  4. ChatGPT discovers the CallRail tools and calls them when a question needs call data.
  5. Every answer cites the account, the window and the fields used to build the number.

docs.title: Setup Guide
docs.text:
1. Sign up at corpusiq.io - the 30-day trial needs no credit card.
  2. Connect CallRail. Dashboard, Connections, CallRail, then approve read access.
  3. Connect ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server per the Quick Start guide.
  4. Verify. Ask "What accounts do I have?" then "How many calls came in last week?" and check both against the CallRail dashboard.
  5. Explore. Then ask the question the dashboard cannot answer: which source produced the calls worth answering.

{

docs.title: How to Connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Cosmos DB is usually where the high-volume records live: event logs, telemetry, user activity, IoT readings. It is written to constantly and read almost never, because reading it means writing queries.

Connecting Cosmos DB through CorpusIQ MCP puts a read-only query path behind a plain-English question. You ask how many events of a type arrived last week, and the connector runs the query against your container and reports back.

CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: Why Connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT?
docs.text:
• Container visibility. "List the containers in my Cosmos database" without opening the portal.
  • Field discovery. Sample-based field shapes and sample values, so you can see what is queryable before writing anything.
  • Distinct counts. "How many distinct event types did we see, grouped by day?" as a sentence.
  • Ad-hoc SELECT. Arbitrary read queries against the container you configured.
  • Health checks. "Is my Cosmos connection healthy?" answered from the connector itself.
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Azure Cosmos DB to CorpusIQ. Enter the endpoint, database and container, then choose key or AAD authentication.
  2. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT as an MCP server, using the endpoint from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ translates the question into read-only queries against your event and telemetry data and assembles the result.
  4. ChatGPT answers from that result and names the objects each figure came from.
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: Before you connect
docs.text:
• An Azure Cosmos DB account using the SQL API
  • The endpoint URL, database name and container name
  • Either the primary key, or an AAD identity holding the Cosmos DB Data Reader role
  • About 3 minutes
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. In CorpusIQ, open Dashboard then Connectors and find Azure Cosmos DB.
  2. Click Configure.
  3. Enter your endpoint, for example https://yourdb.documents.azure.com:443/, plus the database name and container name.
  4. Choose the auth method: Key pastes the primary key from the Azure portal, AAD takes the user principal and tenant ID.
  5. Click Save. The connector turns from gray to green once the first query succeeds.

In ChatGPT

  1. Install CorpusIQ from the ChatGPT app store, or add the CorpusIQ MCP server under Settings, Connectors.
  2. Approve the CorpusIQ authorization when prompted, once.
  3. Start a new conversation and ask a question that needs your data.

If the connector does not appear, work through the Quick Start guide before changing anything else.
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: Example ChatGPT Questions
docs.text:
Discovery

  • "List the containers in my Cosmos database."
  • "What fields does my events container have?"
  • "Show me sample values for the event_type field."

Volume and shape

  • "How many distinct event types did we see, grouped by day?"
  • "How many documents arrived in the last 24 hours?"
  • "Run this query against Cosmos: SELECT TOP 10 c.event_type, c.timestamp FROM c WHERE c.user_id = 'abc'"

Operational

  • "Is my Cosmos connection healthy?"
  • "Which containers are getting the most writes this week?"
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read-only container access. The connector exposes reads: connection status, container listing, sample field insight, distinct-value counts and SELECT queries.
  • No document writes. It never inserts, updates, or deletes documents.
  • Two auth paths. A primary key works, or an AAD identity scoped to the Cosmos DB Built-in Data Reader role. The AAD path keeps a long-lived key out of the picture.
  • Revocable at any time. Rotate the key in the Azure portal, or remove the role assignment, and the connection stops working.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: Comparison: the native interface vs Azure Cosmos DB through ChatGPT
docs.text: Question The native interface CorpusIQ MCP with ChatGPT Input A SQL query and knowledge of the document shape A question in plain language Output Raw documents An answer with the query and the shape named Discovery Data Explorer, container by container Fields and sample values asked for directly Write path Full SDK or portal access None exposed to the assistant
tags: connect Azure Cosmos DB to ChatGPT

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Which Cosmos API does this support? The SQL API. Accounts built on the MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin or Table APIs are a different query surface and are not what this connector targets. Key auth or AAD - which should I use? AAD if your tenant already manages access centrally: the service account needs the Cosmos DB Built-in Data Reader role on the database, which is a data-plane role, not just an RBAC assignment on the account. Key auth is faster to set up and easier to rotate. 401 Unauthorized. What is wrong? The key is wrong or has been rotated. Fetch the current primary key from the Azure portal under the account's Keys blade and re-enter it. AAD authentication keeps failing. Why? The identity needs the Cosmos DB Built-in Data Reader role on the database itself. An RBAC role on the account is not the same permission and will not open the data plane. Cross-partition errors on some queries. What do I do? Some queries have to fan out across partitions. Toggle `cross_partition` in the connection settings for a partitioned container. Can the assistant write or delete documents? No. The connector runs reads and SELECT queries. Inserts, updates, deletes and container changes stay in your application, where they are tested and reviewed.

docs.title: How to Connect Gmail to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Gmail account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting Gmail to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live Gmail data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query your live Gmail inbox - search messages, read email content, and retrieve threads using Gmail's powerful search syntax. You ask questions in plain English and get cited answers from your actual email history in real time.

This page covers the connection architecture, what you can ask, email intelligence use cases, security, and how MCP compares to Gmail's built-in search and Gmail API.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What email questions can I ask ChatGPT about Gmail?  Search questions: "Find all emails from Acme Corp this month", "Search my inbox for messages about the Q3 budget", "Show me emails with attachments from John", "Find any emails about the contract renewal from the last 30 days." Content questions: "What did the client say about the delivery timeline?", "Summarize the email thread about the pricing discussion", "Extract the action items from the project kickoff email." Relationship questions: "When did I last email the Stripe account team?", "Show me my email thread with the HubSpot integration contact", "How many emails have I exchanged with Vendor X this quarter?" Attachment questions: "Find the latest contract from Client Y", "What proposals did I receive this week?", "Show me all invoices sent to me this month."  How does the connection work?  CorpusIQ connects to your Gmail account via Google OAuth 2.0 with read-only scopes. You authenticate with your Google account, authorize Gmail read access, then connect the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. ChatGPT discovers tools for listing messages, searching with Gmail syntax, reading message content, and retrieving threads. The MCP server handles Gmail API pagination, message decoding, and attachment metadata.  Is the connection read-only?  Yes. CorpusIQ requests read-only Gmail scopes: gmail.readonly. ChatGPT can search, list, and read emails. It cannot send emails, delete messages, modify labels, change settings, or perform any write operation in your Gmail account. The advertised Gmail retrieval tools are marked read-only. Write-capable tools, when available, are separately named and annotated.  What Gmail data can ChatGPT access?  Email messages with sender, recipients, subject, date, body content, and labels. Email threads with full conversation history. Attachment metadata (filenames, types, sizes - content reading is available for text-based attachments in supported formats). Gmail labels and categorization. All messages the authenticated user has access to in their Gmail account.  How does ChatGPT search Gmail - do I need to learn Gmail search syntax?  You don't need to learn Gmail search syntax, but it's available if you want precision. You can ask "Find emails from john@example.com with attachments from this month" in natural language, and ChatGPT constructs the equivalent Gmail search query (`from:john@example.com has:attachment newer_than:30d`). You get the precision of Gmail search syntax without needing to learn it. If you already know Gmail search operators, you can use them directly in your questions.  Can ChatGPT summarize long email threads?  Yes - this is one of the most powerful capabilities. "Summarize the 40-message thread about the API migration decision" reads the entire thread and produces a summary with key points, decision outcomes, and action items. What would take 15 minutes of reading becomes a 5-second ChatGPT answer.  Can ChatGPT extract structured information from emails?  Yes. "Extract all dates, amounts, and vendor names from the invoices in my inbox this month." "List all action items assigned to me from emails this week." "Pull all shipping addresses from order confirmation emails." ChatGPT reads email content and extracts structured data from unstructured email text.  Can ChatGPT combine Gmail data with other business tools?  Absolutely - this is where MCP transforms email from an isolated communication tool to a connected business intelligence source. "Show me Gmail conversations with customers who have open HubSpot deals." "Find vendor emails about invoices that match overdue QuickBooks bills." "Search for client feedback emails and cross-reference with their recent Shopify orders." "What internal Gmail discussions reference the Jira issues that are blocking the current sprint?" Email becomes connected to your CRM, financials, ecommerce, and project tools. This cross-source capability is unique to [MCP platforms like CorpusIQ](benefits-of-mcp-for-business.md).  How is this different from Gmail's built-in search?  Gmail's built-in search is keyword-based and returns message lists. It doesn't read message content and synthesize answers. With ChatGPT connected via MCP, you can ask "What did the client decide about the delivery schedule?" and get an answer extracted from the email body - not just a list of matching messages. ChatGPT reads the actual email content, understands context, and answers your question directly.  What about privacy - can ChatGPT see all my emails?  ChatGPT reads emails only in response to questions you ask. Google's OAuth consent screen shows the exact read-only permissions, and you can revoke access from Google Account security settings at any time. Direct MCP requests fetch Gmail records live; CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Gmail to CorpusIQ. Dashboard → Connections → Google Workspace / Gmail → sign into Google → authorize gmail.readonly scope. Takes 2 minutes.

  2. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server. ChatGPT discovers tools for listing messages, searching with Gmail syntax, reading message content, and retrieving threads.

  3. Ask email questions. ChatGPT translates your natural language into Gmail search queries, retrieves matching messages, reads content, and returns cited answers.

  4. Drill down. "Show me the full thread" or "What did they reply?" - follow-ups maintain context across your email history.

No Gmail search syntax required. No inbox scrolling. No manual thread reading.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Conversational email intelligence. Instead of searching Gmail for keywords and manually reading through results, ask "What's the status of the vendor negotiation?" ChatGPT finds the relevant threads and synthesizes an answer.

Thread summarization at scale. "Summarize the top 5 longest email threads from this week." "Give me the key points from the Q3 planning thread." Long email threads that would take 20 minutes to read become 10-second summaries.

Cross-source relationship intelligence. "Show me email communication with our top 10 HubSpot customers this month." "Find vendor emails related to overdue QuickBooks invoices." "What email feedback have we received from customers who recently placed large Shopify orders?" Email patterns become connected to business data from your entire tool stack.

Automated information extraction. "Extract all meeting times proposed in emails this week." "List every budget number mentioned in emails from the finance team." Information buried in email bodies becomes structured and actionable.

Meeting and call preparation. "What email conversations have I had with Acme Corp in the last 30 days?" Arrive at meetings with complete email context - no manual inbox searching.

docs.text: "Summarize all email communication with Client X this month." "What issues has Client Y raised via email?" "Show me the full history of the contract negotiation thread." Account managers get complete client email context in seconds.

docs.title: Vendor and Procurement Management
docs.text: "Find all emails from vendors about price changes this quarter." "Show me the email thread about the software license renewal." "What vendors have emailed about overdue payments?" Vendor relationship management from email history.

docs.title: Executive Summaries
docs.text: "Summarize the key themes from my inbox this week." "What decisions were made via email that I need to know about?" "Which emails require my urgent attention based on content?" Executive email intelligence without reading every message.

docs.title: Cross-Source Intelligence
docs.text: "Find emails from HubSpot deal contacts and show me their current deal status." "Show me customer emails about refunds and cross-reference with Stripe refund data." "What email discussions reference the Jira issues in the current sprint?" Email connected to your business data stack.

docs.title: Security: Read-Only by Google Scope Design
docs.text:
The Gmail integration's security is enforced by Google's own permission system:

  • OAuth 2.0 with gmail.readonly scope. This scope explicitly excludes any write, send, delete, or modify capabilities.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS 1.3 Encryption. All data in transit between Gmail, CorpusIQ, and ChatGPT is encrypted.
  • Google Account Controls. Revoke access at any time from your Google Account → Security → Third-party apps with account access.
  • Consent Screen Transparency. Google's OAuth consent screen shows exactly which permissions are granted - gmail.readonly only.

For individuals and organizations concerned about email privacy, Gmail remains the authoritative source. CorpusIQ retrieves permitted email content through direct MCP; scoped operational retention applies and access can be revoked.

docs.title: How to Connect Gmail to Claude with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your inbox is where decisions, commitments, and vendor terms actually live. The problem is that Gmail is a search box, not an analyst. It finds messages. It does not read forty replies and tell you what was agreed.

Connecting Gmail to Claude through CorpusIQ MCP closes that gap. You ask a question in plain language, Claude reads the messages that answer it, and the answer comes back with the source threads named. No exports. No CSV. No scrolling.

docs.title: Why Connect Gmail to Claude?
docs.text:
Email is the least structured system most businesses run on, and the hardest to query across. Claude gives you a natural language layer over it.

  • Thread summarization. "Summarize the thread about the renewal terms." Claude reads every message in the thread, not just the top result.
  • Commitment tracking. "What did we promise Acme about the delivery date?" The answer is in an email from six weeks ago. Claude finds it.
  • Structured extraction. "List every invoice amount mentioned in emails this month." Unstructured email text becomes a table.
  • Relationship history. "When did we last hear from this vendor?" One question instead of fifteen searches.
  • Cross-source context. Pair email with CRM, billing, or order data in the same conversation, so correspondence and records get checked against each other.
  • Read-only by scope. Gmail access is gmail.readonly. Claude can search and read. It cannot send, delete, or relabel anything.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Gmail to CorpusIQ through Google OAuth, authorizing the read-only Gmail scope.
  2. Connect CorpusIQ to Claude as an MCP server, using the config block from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ translates your question into Gmail searches, retrieves the matching messages and threads, and decodes the bodies.
  4. Claude answers from that retrieved content, with the messages it used.

CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. Log in and open Connectors.
  2. Select Gmail (or the Google Workspace connector if you want Calendar, Drive, and Sheets alongside it).
  3. Sign in to Google and approve the read-only Gmail scope.
  4. Copy the MCP config block shown under Settings, Integrations, Claude Desktop.

In Claude Desktop

  1. Open Settings, Developer, Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Add the CorpusIQ entry:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "corpusiq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Save the file and fully quit Claude Desktop. Not just the window: quit the application.
  2. Reopen Claude, complete the device login when prompted, and the tools indicator appears next to the message box.

If the tools indicator does not appear, work through Claude can't see CorpusIQ before changing anything else.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Google-enforced read scope. The connection requests gmail.readonly, a scope Google itself defines as read-only. There is no send, delete, or modify path.
  • Revocable at any time. Google Account, Security, Third-party access. Revoking there ends the connection.
  • Consent screen transparency. Google shows exactly what is granted, and it is one read scope, not a bundle of write scopes.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. Raw customer files and full connector payloads are not retained. Operational logs keep query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS in transit between Gmail, CorpusIQ, and Claude.

docs.text:
Aspect Gmail search CorpusIQ MCP with Claude Input Keywords and operators A question in plain language Output A list of matching messages A synthesized answer with the sources named Reading You open each message Claude reads the bodies and threads Long threads Manual scrolling Summarized with owners and open items Extraction Copy and paste into a spreadsheet Returned as structured text Cross-source Gmail only Email plus CRM, billing, orders Write access Yes, by you None, read-only scope

Gmail search is the right tool when you know which message you want. Claude is the right tool when you know which question you have.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Can Claude send or delete email through this connection? No. The connection uses Google's read-only Gmail scope. Claude searches, lists, and reads messages. It cannot send, delete, archive, relabel, or change settings. Any write-capable tool, where one exists, is named separately and annotated. Which Gmail accounts can I connect? Each account is authorized independently, so a work account and a personal account can both be connected without sharing a login. Access follows the Google account you approve on the consent screen. Do I need to learn Gmail search operators? No. Ask in plain language and Claude builds the underlying query. If you already know operators such as `from:`, `has:attachment`, or `newer_than:`, you can put them in your question and they are used directly. Can Claude read attachments? Attachment metadata is available, and text-based attachments in supported formats can be read. Binary formats are referenced rather than parsed. How current is the data? Every question is answered against the mailbox at the moment you ask. There is no nightly copy of your inbox behind the answers. Does this work with Google Workspace accounts? Yes, where the Workspace administrator permits third-party OAuth apps. If the admin has restricted app access, the consent screen is blocked at the Google layer and the fix is on the Workspace side, not in Claude.

docs.text:
A Perplexity thread is good at the public record. It is blind to the part of the record that arrived by email: the price change a supplier mentioned on a Tuesday, the delivery date a customer agreed to, the clause nobody put in the contract.

Connecting Gmail through CorpusIQ MCP puts your own correspondence inside the same thread, read-only. You ask a question, Perplexity reads the messages that answer it, and the answer names the threads it used.

docs.title: Why Connect Gmail to Perplexity?
docs.text:
• The internal half of a research question. "What did this supplier tell us about lead times before the shortage was public?" needs your mailbox and the web in one answer.
  • Commitments, not keywords. Gmail search returns messages that match words. It will not tell you which promise is still open.
  • Across threads. A single deal usually spans four conversations with three domains. The question is about the deal, not about one thread.
  • Numbers buried in prose. Amounts, dates and quantities sit inside sentences. Asked properly, they come back as a list.
  • Read-only by scope. The connector holds gmail.readonly. There is no send, delete or relabel path from either assistant.
  • Silence is an answer. "Which customers have not replied since the quote?" is a question about what is missing, and it is answerable here.

1. Connect Gmail to CorpusIQ with Google OAuth, approving the read-only Gmail scope. The same connection can cover Google Calendar, Drive and Sheets if you want them in the same thread.
  2. Add CorpusIQ to Perplexity as a custom remote MCP server, using the endpoint from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ turns the question into Gmail searches, pulls the matching messages and threads, and decodes the bodies.
  4. Perplexity answers from what came back, and names the period and the threads it measured.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational query logs are kept for up to 30 days.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Can Perplexity send an email on my behalf? No. The connection is read-only, and no tool in the Gmail connector can send, delete or change a label. Does this read my whole mailbox? It can read anything the approved Google account can read, because that is what the scope means. It reads only what a question requires. Raw customer files and full connector response payloads are not retained; operational logs are kept for up to 30 days. Why does it find nothing when Gmail search does? Two usual causes. The question was phrased as a search instead of a question, or the Search Console style operators people type into Gmail do not translate. Ask for the thing you want to know, not the words you would type. Can it read attachments? It reads attachment metadata and the text of common document and spreadsheet formats. A scanned PDF with no text layer comes back as a file reference, not as content. Does this work only in Perplexity? No. Gmail is exposed to ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity through the same endpoint on the same subscription. Where is the email data stored? docs.title: How to Connect Google Ads to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Google Ads account holds the spend, the search terms, and the quality scores that decide what everything costs. Reading it normally means the web interface, one report and one date range at a time. Connecting Google Ads to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP changes that: you authorize read-only access once, and ChatGPT answers questions from your live account in plain English, with the figures cited.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query campaigns, ad groups, keywords, search terms, quality scores, device and geographic breakdowns, and spend metrics, so you can interrogate the account rather than page through it.

docs.title: What you can ask
docs.text:
• "Which campaigns spent the most last month, and what did each return?"
  • "Which search terms triggered ads but never converted, and how much did they cost?"
  • "Where is quality score lowest, and is it the ad relevance or the landing page?"
  • "How does mobile spend and conversion compare with desktop this quarter?"
  • "Which ad groups are bidding on terms we already rank organically for?"
  • "What is our cost per conversion trend over the last six months?"
  • "Which campaigns have spent with no conversions in the last 30 days?"

docs.title: What Google Ads data CorpusIQ reaches
docs.text:
• Campaign performance. Spend, impressions, clicks, and conversions over any date range.
  • Ad groups and ads. Performance at the level where budget actually gets decided.
  • Keywords. Bids, match types, quality scores, and performance per keyword.
  • Search terms. The actual queries that triggered your ads, including the ones that never converted.
  • Quality score components. Ad relevance, expected click-through rate, and landing page experience.
  • Device and geography. Where spend and conversions come from by device and by location.

docs.title: Agency and multi-account use
docs.text:
If you manage client accounts, you can connect a single manager account identity and have the linked client accounts discovered automatically, so one connection answers questions across the accounts you manage instead of one at a time.

That makes the cross-client question possible:

  • "Which of my client accounts had the biggest month-on-month increase in cost per conversion?"
  • "Which accounts have campaigns spending with no conversions this month?"
  • "Rank the accounts by wasted spend on non-converting search terms."

docs.title: Cross-source questions
docs.text:
The most useful Google Ads questions cross into the rest of the business, which is what MCP is for:

  • "Compare Google Ads cost per acquisition with Meta Ads for the same period."
  • "Does the revenue Google Ads reports match what our commerce platform actually booked?"
  • "Which campaigns drove orders from customers with the highest lifetime value?"
  • "How does paid search performance compare with email revenue this quarter?"

Those answers come from your ads connection together with your analytics, commerce, and finance connections.

docs.title: How the connection works
docs.text:
CorpusIQ connects to Google Ads using the provider's own OAuth authorization. You grant read-only access on the consent screen, connect the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity, and the assistant calls the Google Ads retrieval tools when a question needs them.

The connection is assistant-agnostic. You connect the account once and use it from any MCP-capable client.

docs.title: Security and data handling
docs.text:
• Read-only. The Google Ads retrieval tools are marked read-only. The assistant can read and cite account data, but it cannot change bids, budgets, campaigns, or creatives.
  • Bounded, scoped retention. Direct MCP requests fetch live and do not build a raw-file or full-payload warehouse. Scoped operational logs may persist for up to 30 days.
  • Your access controls. Nobody at CorpusIQ can access your accounts, and each user queries under their own authorized credentials.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Can ChatGPT change my bids or pause a campaign?  No. The retrieval tools documented here are marked read-only. The assistant can analyse and cite your Google Ads data, but it cannot modify bids, budgets, or campaign settings. Those changes stay in Google Ads.   Is this a replacement for the Google Ads interface?  No, it is a different way of asking. The interface is built for looking; this is built for asking the cross-system question, such as whether paid search revenue matches booked revenue.   Do you support manager accounts for agencies?  Yes. You can connect a manager account identity and have linked client accounts discovered automatically, so one connection covers the accounts you manage.   How current is the data?  CorpusIQ queries Google Ads through the live API, so recent spend and conversion changes show up in your next question. Note that Google Ads reporting data itself can lag by a few hours, which is a platform behaviour rather than a CorpusIQ delay.   Can I compare Google Ads with Meta Ads in one question?  Yes. With both connected, "compare cost per acquisition across Google Ads and Meta Ads this quarter" is a single question rather than two exports and a spreadsheet.   What level of access do I need?  You need access to the Google Ads account that grants permission to authorize the connection. The scopes requested are shown on Google's consent screen before you approve them.

docs.title: How to Connect Google Analytics to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Google Analytics account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting Google Analytics to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live Google Analytics data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query your live GA4 data - traffic, sessions, users, conversions, and ecommerce revenue. You ask questions in plain English and get answers from your actual analytics property, not exported spreadsheets or outdated dashboards.

This page covers the connection architecture, what you can ask, cross-source capabilities, security, and how MCP compares to using GA4's native interface or API.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What web analytics questions can I ask ChatGPT?  Traffic questions: "What was our total website traffic last week?", "Which pages got the most views this month?", "How many users did we have yesterday?" Conversion questions: "What's our conversion rate for the last 30 days?", "Which traffic source has the highest conversion rate?" Ecommerce questions: "What was our ecommerce revenue from organic search this month?", "Show me revenue by product category." Campaign questions: "How much traffic did our latest email campaign drive?", "Which ad campaigns generated the most conversions?"  How does CorpusIQ connect GA4 to ChatGPT?  CorpusIQ connects to your Google Analytics account via OAuth 2.0. You select which GA4 property to connect, authorize read-only access, then connect the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. ChatGPT discovers the available analytics tools and calls them when you ask a question. The MCP server handles the GA4 Data API, dimension/metric mapping, and date range construction automatically.  What GA4 data can ChatGPT access?  Traffic metrics: sessions, users, new users, pageviews, screen views. Engagement metrics: average engagement time, engaged sessions, bounce rate. Conversion metrics: conversions, conversion rate, event count. Ecommerce metrics: purchase revenue, transactions, item revenue, add-to-carts. All broken down by dimensions like date, source/medium, country, device category, landing page, and campaign.  Is this read-only?  Yes. The Google Analytics API is inherently read-only - it provides analytics data, not configuration access. CorpusIQ requests the minimum OAuth scopes needed to read analytics data. ChatGPT cannot modify your GA4 property settings, create events, or alter tracking configuration.  Can ChatGPT compare GA4 data with data from other tools?  This is where MCP creates value beyond what GA4 alone can offer. "Did our Google Ads campaigns drive more revenue than our email campaigns this month?" queries GA4 for conversion data, Google Ads for spend data, and Klaviyo for email campaign data - all in one response. "How does our website traffic correlate with Shopify orders?" combines GA4 and Shopify data. Cross-source analytics is the core capability of [MCP platforms like CorpusIQ](benefits-of-mcp-for-business.md).  How is this different from using GA4's built-in reports?  GA4's built-in reports are pre-constructed views with specific dimensions and metrics. They're useful for standard analysis but limit you to what Google decided to include. With ChatGPT, every question is a custom report: "Show me the bounce rate for mobile users from paid search who landed on product pages" is a question you'd struggle to build in GA4's interface but can ask naturally in ChatGPT. You're not limited to pre-built reports - you ask exactly what you need.  How does this handle GA4's event-based data model?  GA4's event-based model is powerful but complex. Events have parameters, and understanding which event maps to which business metric requires GA4 expertise. CorpusIQ's MCP layer abstracts this complexity. You ask about "conversions" or "purchases" in natural language, and the MCP server maps to the correct GA4 events and parameters. You don't need to know the event names or parameter keys.  What about real-time data?  CorpusIQ supports GA4's real-time reporting. You can ask "How many active users are on our site right now?" or "What pages are real-time users viewing?" This real-time capability lets you monitor campaign launches, product releases, or promotional events as they happen.  Can I query multiple GA4 properties?  Yes. Connect multiple GA4 properties to CorpusIQ. Compare traffic across properties, or combine data for a portfolio view: "Show me total traffic across all our properties this month."  What about historical data?  GA4 properties have a data retention setting (2 months or 14 months by default). CorpusIQ can query any data within your property's retention window. For data beyond the retention window, you'd need BigQuery export - a topic covered in our [GA4 connector reference](connect-google-analytics-to-chatgpt.md).

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Can Claude edit or move files in my Drive? No. The connection is read-only. Claude can search and read files the connected account can open. It cannot create, edit, move, share, or delete anything in Drive. Does it read PDFs and Word documents? Text-based formats are read, which covers the common business set: Docs, PDFs with a text layer, Word files, plain text, and spreadsheets. Scanned images without a text layer are referenced rather than parsed, because there is no text to read. How does it handle multiple versions of the same document? Ask for the current one explicitly: "the latest signed version of the Acme agreement". The connector reads files as they stand, so a document edited this morning is what the next answer sees. When two files could match, the answer names the file it used so you can check it. Can it read files in shared drives? Yes, where the connected account has access to that shared drive. Access follows the Google account you approved, and the shared drive's own restrictions still apply. Can it combine Drive with my CRM or accounting? Yes. This is where document search stops being a search box. "Does the contract match what the CRM says about this account?" is one question across both sources instead of two manual checks. How current is the data? Live. Files are read at the moment you ask. Raw customer files are not retained, and scoped operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. Where is my document data stored? CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Retrieval happens on demand. Operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. Where is my data stored?  It is not. Retrieval happens on demand against the live API. CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. docs.text:
Most businesses run a second, unofficial database in Google Sheets: the budget, the hiring plan, the pipeline tracker, the inventory count that someone updates on Fridays. The data is real, and it is invisible to every other system. Connecting Google Sheets to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP makes those sheets queryable with a plain-English question, read-only, answered from the sheet as it stands.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only and does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational query logs are retained for up to 30 days.

docs.title: What Questions Can You Ask?
docs.text:
• "What is total spend in the Q4 budget tab, by category?"
  • "Which deals in the pipeline tracker have not moved in 30 days?"
  • "Sum the headcount plan by department and compare it to actual."
  • "Which rows in the inventory count are below the reorder threshold?"
  • "What changed in this sheet compared with last month?"

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: Is this read-only?  Yes. The connector reads spreadsheets and leaves them untouched. It cannot edit cells, add rows, or change sharing. If a workflow needs a write path, that is a separate decision with a separate credential.  Which spreads come through, the whole file or a tab?  You point the connector at a spreadsheet and it can read its tabs and ranges. For a large workbook, naming the tab in the question gives the tightest, fastest answer: "the FY26 budget tab" rather than "the budget file".  Do merged cells and formulas break it?  Formulas are read as their computed values, which is what you want. Merged cells and multi-row headers are the usual source of a wrong answer, because the header no longer labels the right column. If a sheet is heavily formatted, adding a clean tab with a single header row fixes it in a minute.  Can it combine sheets with QuickBooks or Stripe?  Yes, and this is the strongest use for a Sheets connector. The budget lives in a sheet and the actuals live in QuickBooks. "Compare budget to actual by category for last quarter" is one question across both, instead of a manual reconciliation.  Does my whole Drive get exposed?  No. The Sheets connector reads spreadsheet data. Drive appears as a separate connector, and Google's consent screen lists the read-only permissions being requested (Drive, Sheets, Gmail, Analytics and the rest of the Google surfaces you enable) for you to approve in one place. You can revoke any of them later from your Google Account security settings. Connect only what a question would actually use.  How current is the data?  Live. When you ask, the connector reads the sheet as it stands. If someone typed a number a minute ago, the next question sees it.  What about shared sheets owned by someone else?  Access follows the Google account you authorize with. If that account can open the sheet, the connector can read it. If the sheet is shared as a link with restricted access, that restriction still applies.  Where is my data stored?  CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Retrieval happens on demand. Operational query logs may persist for up to 30 days. See our [security documentation](../security/) for the detail.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. You connect Google Sheets in the CorpusIQ dashboard and approve the read scope on Google's consent screen.
  2. You add the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. See the Quick Start guide.
  3. ChatGPT discovers the Sheets tools and calls them when a question needs spreadsheet data.
  4. Answers cite the spreadsheet, tab, and range used.

  2. Connect Google Sheets. Dashboard, Connections, Google Sheets, then approve the read scope.
  3. Connect ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server per the Quick Start guide.

docs.title: How to Connect Google Sheets to Claude with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Half of a business lives in spreadsheets nobody designed as a database. The budget, the hiring plan, the pipeline tracker, the inventory count somebody updates on Fridays.

Claude can read that data and answer questions about it, but only if the data reaches Claude. Copying a tab into a chat works once and is stale by the next question.

Connecting Google Sheets through CorpusIQ MCP closes that gap. You ask a question, Claude reads the sheet as it stands, and the answer names the spreadsheet and the tab it came from.

docs.title: Why Connect Google Sheets to Claude?
docs.text:
• Questions over formulas. "Which cost centres are over budget this quarter?" instead of building another pivot.
  • Tracker reads. "Which deals in the pipeline tracker have not moved in 30 days?"
  • Reconciliation. "Compare the budget sheet to actuals in the accounting system, by category." Two sources, one question.
  • Change detection. "What changed in the hiring plan since the last version?"
  • Threshold checks. "Which SKUs in the inventory count are below the reorder point?"
  • Read-only by scope. The connection reads spreadsheets. It cannot edit a cell, add a row, or change sharing.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Google Sheets to CorpusIQ through Google OAuth and approve the read-only scopes on Google's consent screen.
  2. Connect CorpusIQ to Claude as an MCP server, using the config block from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ translates your question into spreadsheet reads, opens the tabs and ranges that answer it, and returns the values.
  4. Claude answers from that retrieved content, naming the sheet and tab used.

CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. Log in and open Connectors.
  2. Select Google Sheets (or the Google Workspace connector if you want Drive, Calendar, and Gmail alongside it).
  3. Sign in to Google and approve the read-only scopes.
  4. Copy the MCP config block shown under Settings, Integrations, Claude Desktop.

In Claude Desktop

  1. Open Settings, Developer, Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Add the CorpusIQ entry:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "corpusiq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Save the file and fully quit Claude Desktop. Not just the window: quit the application.
  2. Reopen Claude, complete the device login when prompted, and the tools indicator appears next to the message box.

If the tools indicator does not appear, work through Claude can't see CorpusIQ before changing anything else.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read scope only. The connection requests Google's read-only spreadsheet scopes. There is no write path from Claude into a sheet.
  • Revocable at any time. Google Account, Security, Third-party access. Revoking there ends the connection.
  • Account-scoped. Access follows the Google account you approve. A sheet that account cannot open stays out of reach.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. Raw customer files and full connector payloads are not retained. Operational logs keep query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS in transit between Google, CorpusIQ, and Claude.

Spreadsheet search is the right tool when you know the row. Claude is the right tool when you know the question.

docs.text:
Can Claude edit my spreadsheet through this connection? No. The connection reads spreadsheet data. Cells, rows, and sharing settings are untouched. Any write-capable path would be a separate decision with a separate credential, and it is not part of this connector. Does the whole file come through, or one tab? The connector can read a spreadsheet's tabs and ranges. For a large workbook, naming the tab in the question gives the tightest answer: "the FY26 budget tab" rather than "the budget file". Do merged cells and formulas break the answers? Formulas come through as their computed values, which is what you want. Merged cells and multi-row headers are the usual cause of a wrong answer, because the header no longer labels the right column. A clean tab with a single header row fixes it in a minute. Can it combine a sheet with QuickBooks or Stripe? Yes, and this is the strongest use of a Sheets connector. The plan lives in a sheet and the actuals live in accounting. "Compare budget to actual by category for last quarter" becomes one question instead of a manual reconciliation. Does connecting Sheets expose my whole Drive? No. Sheets is its own connector. Google's consent screen lists the read-only permissions being requested, and you approve them in one place. Revoke any of them later from your Google Account security settings. Connect only what a question would actually use. How current is the data? Live. When you ask, the connector reads the sheet as it stands. A number typed a minute ago is visible to the next question. There is no nightly copy behind the answers. What about sheets owned by somebody else? Access follows the Google account you authorized. If that account can open the sheet, the connector can read it. A link-restricted share keeps its restriction. Where is my spreadsheet data stored? CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Retrieval happens on demand. Operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. See the [security documentation](../security/) for detail.

docs.title: How to Connect HubSpot to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your HubSpot account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting HubSpot to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live HubSpot data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can search your contacts, list deals by stage, pull full company profiles, and answer questions that span contacts, deals, and companies - all in plain English, all from live HubSpot data.

This page covers the connection architecture, what you can ask, security, setup, and how MCP compares to direct HubSpot API integration.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What CRM questions can I ask ChatGPT about HubSpot?  Questions about contacts, deals, companies, and your pipeline. Examples: "Pull together everything I need to know about Acme Corp", "How many deals are in the negotiation stage?", "Search HubSpot for contacts at Stripe", "Show me my top 10 deals by amount", "Which deals are closing this month?", "What's my pipeline value by stage?", "Show me all contacts created in the last 30 days", "Which deals have been stuck in the same stage for over 2 weeks?", "Give me a summary of all activity with Company X."  How does CorpusIQ connect HubSpot to ChatGPT?  CorpusIQ connects to HubSpot via OAuth 2.0 and exposes HubSpot's CRM objects as MCP tools. You authorize read-only access once (selecting which HubSpot portal to connect), then add the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. When you ask a CRM question, ChatGPT calls the appropriate tool - contact search, deal listing, company retrieval - and returns a cited answer from your live HubSpot data.  Is the connection read-only?  The advertised HubSpot retrieval tools are read-only and expose contacts, deals, and companies without modifying them. Write-capable tools, when available, are separately named and annotated.  What HubSpot objects can ChatGPT access?  Contacts with full property details and keyword search. Companies with full details. Deals with status, stage, amount, and close date. HubSpot account and portal metadata. All accessed through read-only operations - ChatGPT reads your CRM data, it never writes to it.  Can ChatGPT combine HubSpot data with data from other tools?  Yes. This is where MCP creates value that no single-platform dashboard can match. "Show me all deals closing this month and cross-reference with email activity from Gmail" combines HubSpot deal data with Gmail communication history. "Which customers have open deals and overdue invoices?" spans HubSpot and QuickBooks. The cross-source capability is the differentiator - see our [Benefits of MCP for Business](benefits-of-mcp-for-business.md).  How is this different from HubSpot's built-in AI features?  HubSpot's AI features (like Breeze AI) are designed for specific HubSpot-native workflows - content generation, forecasting, email composition. They work within HubSpot's interface and primarily on HubSpot data alone. Connecting HubSpot to ChatGPT via MCP enables ad-hoc natural language queries across your CRM data and any other connected data source. The interface is ChatGPT (where many teams already spend time), and the scope is your entire data stack, not just HubSpot.  What permissions do I need in HubSpot?  You need a HubSpot account with admin access to authorize the OAuth connection. Once authorized, any CorpusIQ user with access to that authorization can query the connected portal through ChatGPT. Free HubSpot accounts may have limited object scopes - some properties may not be accessible.  Can I search across all CRM objects at once?  You can ask questions that span contacts, deals, and companies. "Find every interaction with Company X - contacts, open deals, recent activity." ChatGPT will make multiple MCP tool calls as needed and synthesize the results. This multi-object query capability is built into the MCP architecture.  How does this handle custom properties?  Custom HubSpot properties are included in contact, deal, and company objects. If you've created custom fields in HubSpot, ChatGPT can query and reference them. Just ask: "Show me all deals where the custom field 'Implementation Tier' is 'Enterprise'."  Does this work with multiple HubSpot portals?  Yes. You can connect multiple HubSpot portals to CorpusIQ. Each portal's data is isolated, and you can specify which portal to query - or ask ChatGPT to pull data across portals for multi-brand or multi-region sales analysis.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect HubSpot to CorpusIQ. In your CorpusIQ dashboard, click Connections → HubSpot → sign into HubSpot → select your portal → approve read-only access. Takes 2 minutes.

  2. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server as a connected app in ChatGPT. ChatGPT automatically discovers your available CRM tools.

  3. Ask CRM questions. ChatGPT receives your question, identifies the HubSpot tools it needs, calls them, and returns a cited response from live data.

  4. Iterate conversationally. "Now show me the contacts at those companies" or "Which of those deals are most at risk?" - follow-up questions maintain context.

No ETL pipeline. No data warehouse. No scheduled syncs. Your CRM data is queried live, every time.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Sales pipeline visibility without CRM navigation. Your CEO, finance lead, or board members can ask about pipeline health without logging into HubSpot. "What's our pipeline value by stage?" is a ChatGPT question, not a CRM login session.

Account 360 in one question. Preparing for a customer call? Ask ChatGPT: "Give me everything on Acme Corp - contacts, open deals, deal values, last activity dates." One question replaces clicking through multiple HubSpot screens.

Pipeline management at scale. "Which deals are stalled?" "Show me deals with no activity in 14 days." "Which reps have the most deals in the proposal stage?" Pipeline hygiene questions that would require custom reports in HubSpot become instant queries.

Cross-source relationship intelligence. The real power comes from connecting HubSpot with your other tools. "Show me open deals for customers with overdue invoices" combines HubSpot and QuickBooks. "Which customers with open deals haven't opened our last email campaign?" combines HubSpot and Klaviyo. This cross-source context is unique to MCP platforms like CorpusIQ.

Source-cited answers you can verify. Every response includes provenance - which HubSpot object was queried, when, and what was returned. If a deal amount looks wrong, you can trace it back to the source record.

docs.title: Pre-Call Briefing
docs.text: Before a sales call: "Give me a full brief on Company X - all contacts, open deals, deal amounts, last activity, and any recent email threads." One question, one answer, no tab-switching.

docs.title: Weekly Pipeline Review
docs.text: Instead of building a pipeline report in HubSpot: "Show me all deals by stage with amounts, close dates, and owner. Flag any that are past their expected close date." Your weekly review becomes a conversation.

docs.title: Territory and Rep Performance
docs.text: "How many deals did each rep close this quarter?" "What's the average deal size by rep?" "Which territories have the healthiest pipeline?" Sales leadership gets answers without building reports.

docs.title: Customer Health Scoring
docs.text: "Score my top 20 customers by deal recency, deal size, and email engagement." ChatGPT can retrieve HubSpot deal data, cross-reference with email activity, and calculate a composite health score - all from one prompt.

docs.title: Cross-Source Attribution
docs.text: "Which marketing campaigns generated the most HubSpot deals this quarter?" queries HubSpot for closed deals in the period, then cross-references with Google Ads and Meta Ads for campaign attribution. See our MCP for Marketing guide for more attribution use cases.

docs.title: Security: Read-Only by Design
docs.text:
The advertised HubSpot retrieval surface is read-only:

  • Retrieval tools: Contact search, deal listing, and company retrieval are marked read-only.
  • Other operations: Write-capable tools, when available, are separately named and annotated.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • Encryption: All data in transit is encrypted via TLS 1.3 between HubSpot, CorpusIQ, and ChatGPT.

For sales organizations with strict data-governance requirements, HubSpot remains the authoritative source. CorpusIQ retrieves permitted CRM records through direct MCP; the retention classes and lifecycles described above still apply.

docs.title: Comparison: MCP vs. Direct HubSpot API Integration
docs.text:
Aspect Direct API Integration CorpusIQ MCP Setup Days of development - HubSpot API client, OAuth, pagination, rate limiting 2 minutes - OAuth authorization Query interface REST endpoints, JSON parsing, custom code for each query type Natural language - ask any CRM question Multi-object queries Must code joins across contacts, deals, companies manually Automatic - ChatGPT orchestrates tool calls Cross-source Separate integrations for every tool, custom orchestration layer One question across all connected tools Search HubSpot search syntax, property-specific filters Natural language search with automatic property mapping Maintenance API version updates, property schema changes, token rotation CorpusIQ handles all maintenance

The direct API approach is right when you need write operations - creating contacts programmatically, updating deal stages via workflow, or building custom HubSpot integrations. For CRM data access, Q&A, and reporting, MCP is faster to deploy, safer by default, and instantly cross-source capable.

docs.text:
1. Sign up at corpusiq.io - free 30-day trial.
  2. Connect HubSpot. Dashboard → Connections → HubSpot → sign into HubSpot → select portal → authorize read-only access.
  3. Connect ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. See our Quick Start guide for instructions.
  4. Verify. Ask "How many contacts are in my HubSpot account?" to confirm the connection.
  5. Explore. Try "Show me my open deals sorted by amount" or "Search for contacts at example.com."

Under 5 minutes from signup to your first CRM query in ChatGPT.

Claude eliminates that friction by letting anyone on your team ask natural language questions and receive instant answers from live CRM data.

docs.title: How to Connect Jira to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Jira account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting Jira to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live Jira data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query your live Jira data - issues, sprints, epics, assignees, status transitions, and project velocity. You ask questions in plain English and get cited answers from your Jira instance - no JQL required.

This page covers the connection architecture, what you can ask, agile workflow use cases, security, and how MCP compares to JQL queries and direct Jira API integration.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What development questions can I ask ChatGPT about Jira?  Issue questions: "Show me all open bugs in the current sprint", "What issues are assigned to me?", "Which issues have been in 'In Progress' for more than 5 days?" Sprint questions: "What's the status of Sprint 42?", "How many story points have we completed this sprint?", "What's our velocity over the last 5 sprints?" Epic questions: "What's the status of the Authentication Epic?", "Show me all unresolved issues in Epic X." Release questions: "What issues are targeted for the next release?", "How many bugs are open for the current release?" Team questions: "Who has the most open issues?", "Show me issue distribution by assignee this sprint."  How does the connection work?  CorpusIQ connects to your Jira instance (Cloud or Data Center) via OAuth 2.0 or personal access token. You authorize read-only access, then connect the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. ChatGPT discovers the available Jira tools - issue search, sprint reporting, project listing, and issue retrieval - and calls them when you ask a question. The MCP server handles JQL construction, pagination, and field mapping behind the scenes.  Is the connection read-only?  Yes. CorpusIQ requests read-only permissions from Jira. ChatGPT can see issues, projects, sprints, and reports. It cannot create issues, transition statuses, assign work, comment on issues, or modify anything in your Jira instance. The read-only guarantee is enforced at the Jira permission and MCP tool levels.  What Jira data can ChatGPT access?  Projects and their metadata. Issues with summary, description, status, assignee, priority, labels, components, and custom fields. Sprints with start/end dates, goal, and completion status. Epics with linked issues and progress. All standard and custom fields are accessible - just reference them by name.  Can ChatGPT write JQL for me?  ChatGPT doesn't just write JQL - it eliminates the need for JQL entirely. Instead of writing `project = "PLATFORM" AND status = "In Progress" AND assignee = currentUser() ORDER BY priority DESC`, you ask "Show me my in-progress issues in the Platform project, sorted by priority." ChatGPT translates your natural language into the appropriate JQL, executes it, and returns the results. You get JQL-level precision without learning JQL syntax.  Can ChatGPT combine Jira data with other development tools?  Yes. "Show me Jira issues linked to recent GitHub pull requests" or "Which Jira bugs correspond to production incidents in our monitoring dashboard?" Cross-source development visibility connects your issue tracker with your code repository, CI/CD pipeline, and monitoring tools.  Can ChatGPT combine Jira with business tools?  This is where MCP truly differentiates from Jira-native reporting. "Which Jira epics are associated with HubSpot deals closing this quarter?" "Show me open customer-reported bugs and their corresponding Salesforce cases." "Which features being built this sprint map to the highest-value Shopify products?" Connecting development data to business data provides context that isolated Jira reports cannot.  How is this different from Jira's built-in dashboards?  Jira dashboards are excellent for recurring team-level metrics - burndown charts, velocity, issue distributions. But they answer the questions you anticipate, not the questions you discover. "Show me all issues that were reopened more than twice in the last 30 days" is a JQL query and chart you'd need to build specifically - or a ChatGPT question that takes seconds. MCP complements Jira dashboards with ad-hoc analytical capability.  Does this work with Jira Cloud and Jira Data Center?  Yes. CorpusIQ supports both Jira Cloud (via OAuth 2.0) and Jira Data Center (via personal access tokens). Connection setup differs slightly (OAuth for Cloud, PAT for Data Center), but the ChatGPT experience is identical.  Can I query across multiple Jira projects and boards?  Yes. "Show me all open issues across the Frontend, Backend, and DevOps projects." "What's the combined velocity across all engineering teams this quarter?" "Which projects have the most unresolved bugs?" Multi-project queries work naturally - no need to run separate JQL queries and combine results manually.

docs.text:

No JQL. No board switching. No manual issue compilation.

Development visibility for non-developers. Product managers, executives, and customer-facing teams can ask Jira questions without learning Jira's interface or JQL. "What's the status of Feature X?" is a ChatGPT question anyone can ask.

docs.title: Security: Read-Only by Design
docs.text:
The Jira integration is read-only at every layer:

  • OAuth 2.0 / PAT with read-only permissions. No write, create, transition, or delete permissions.
  • Project Permission Respect. ChatGPT can only see projects and issues the authenticated user has permission to view in Jira.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS 1.3 Encryption. All data in transit is encrypted.

For engineering organizations with sensitive project data, Jira remains the authoritative source. CorpusIQ retrieves permitted Jira records through direct MCP; the retention classes and lifecycles described above still apply.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. Open Settings, Developer, Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Add the CorpusIQ entry:
{

      "args": [

      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Save the file and fully quit Claude Desktop. Not just the window: quit the application.
  2. Reopen Claude, complete the device login when prompted, and the tools indicator appears next to the message box.

If the tools indicator does not appear, work through Claude can't see CorpusIQ before changing anything else.

docs.text:
• Read-only by permission. The connection requests read access to projects, issues, sprints, and reports. There is no path for Claude to create an issue, transition a status, assign work, or comment.
  • Enforced in two places. The Jira permission scope and the MCP tool set both refuse writes, so a write attempt fails rather than silently succeeding.
  • Revocable at any time. Removing the CorpusIQ application in Jira, or revoking the personal access token, ends the connection immediately.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Does this work with Jira Data Center, or only Cloud? Both. Jira Cloud authorizes through OAuth. Data Center authorizes with a personal access token issued to the account you want read. In both cases the access is read-only. Do I need to know JQL? No. Ask in plain language and CorpusIQ builds the underlying search. If you already know JQL, you can paste a query into your question and it is used directly. Can Claude change an issue status or assign work? No. Every Jira tool exposed to Claude is read-only. Creating issues, transitioning statuses, assigning, commenting, and editing fields are not available through this connection. Which Jira projects can Claude see? Only the projects the authorizing account can already see in Jira. Permissions are inherited from the account, so Claude cannot reach a project that the human who connected it could not open. Are custom fields available? Yes. Standard fields come back with each issue, and custom fields can be referenced by name in your question. Story point fields, team fields, and internal priority fields all work. How current is the data? Every question is answered against the instance at the moment you ask. There is no nightly copy of your Jira project behind the answers.
