docs.title: How to Connect Klaviyo to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Klaviyo account holds the email and SMS revenue for your store, plus the flows and segments behind it. Reading it normally means clicking through dashboards one report at a time. Connecting Klaviyo to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP removes that step: you authorize read-only access once, and ChatGPT answers questions from your live Klaviyo data in plain English, citing the source.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query campaigns, flows, abandoned cart performance, list growth, subscriber health, and revenue attribution directly, so the answer reflects the account as it stands right now.

docs.title: What you can ask
docs.text:
Because the connection reaches live data, the questions can be specific rather than dashboard-shaped:

  • "Which flows generated the most revenue in the last 30 days, and what is each one's revenue per recipient?"
  • "How did this month's campaigns compare with the same month last year?"
  • "Which segments have the highest unsubscribe rate, and what is driving it?"
  • "What is our abandoned cart recovery rate, and how has it moved this quarter?"
  • "How fast is the list growing, and what share of new subscribers came from popups versus checkout?"
  • "Which campaign subject lines performed best by open rate?"
  • "Show me revenue attributed to email versus SMS this month."

docs.title: What Klaviyo data CorpusIQ reaches
docs.text:
• Campaigns. Performance, engagement, and revenue attribution over any date range.
  • Flows. Flow-level revenue, recipient counts, and conversion performance.
  • Abandoned cart. Recovery volume and revenue from cart and browse abandonment.
  • List growth. Subscriber counts and growth over time.
  • Subscriber health. Engagement and deliverability signals across the list.
  • Forms and signup sources. Where subscribers came from and how each source performs.

docs.title: Cross-source questions
docs.text:
The most valuable Klaviyo questions are the ones that cross into another system, which is where MCP does what no single dashboard can:

  • "Does our Shopify revenue match what Klaviyo attributes to email for the same period?"
  • "Which email-attributed customers also made a purchase on Amazon this quarter?"
  • "Is our ad spend on Meta producing subscribers who later buy, or just subscribers?"
  • "How does email revenue compare with paid channel revenue over the last 90 days?"

Those questions are answered from Klaviyo and your commerce, ad, and finance connections together.

docs.title: How the connection works
docs.text:
CorpusIQ connects to Klaviyo through the provider's own OAuth authorization. You authorize the connection once and choose the scopes on the provider's consent screen. The CorpusIQ MCP server then exposes Klaviyo retrieval to ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity, and the assistant calls those tools when your question needs them.

The same connection works across assistants. You connect the data once rather than rebuilding the integration per tool.

docs.title: Security and data handling
docs.text:
• Read-only. The Klaviyo retrieval tools documented here are marked read-only. The assistant can read and cite your marketing data, but it cannot send a campaign, edit a flow, or modify a subscriber.
  • Bounded, scoped retention. Direct MCP requests fetch live and do not build a raw-file or full-payload warehouse. Scoped operational logs may persist for up to 30 days.
  • Your access controls. Nobody at CorpusIQ can access your accounts. Each user connects and queries under their own authorized credentials.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Can ChatGPT send a campaign or edit a flow?  No. The retrieval tools documented here are marked read-only. The assistant can read and cite Klaviyo data, but it cannot create, send, or modify anything in your account. Campaign execution stays in Klaviyo.   Is this different from the Klaviyo dashboard?  Yes. The dashboard shows you the reports Klaviyo decided to build. MCP lets you ask the cross-source question, such as comparing Klaviyo-attributed revenue with actual order data, which no single dashboard answers.   How current is the data?  CorpusIQ queries Klaviyo through the live API. A campaign that finished an hour ago is reflected in your next question. There is no overnight refresh and no ETL lag.   Does this work with SMS as well as email?  Yes. The Klaviyo connector covers email and SMS campaign and flow performance, so both channels are queryable in the same answer.   Which other assistants can use this connection?  CorpusIQ is an MCP server, so the same connection serves ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity, and any other MCP-capable client you use.   Do I need a Klaviyo enterprise plan?  You need an account with API access and the permission level required to authorize the connection. CorpusIQ connects through Klaviyo's own OAuth flow, and the required scopes are shown on the consent screen.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:

  2. Give it read scopes on Campaigns, Flows, Lists, Segments, Profiles, Metrics, Forms, and Events.

In CorpusIQ

  2. Paste the private key and save.

In Perplexity

  1. Open Settings and find the MCP servers section.
  2. Add a custom MCP server and paste the endpoint:
https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp
  1. Connect and approve the CorpusIQ authorization page once.
  2. Start a new thread and ask a revenue question.

A 403 Forbidden on the first question means the key is missing a read scope. Recreate it with every scope listed above rather than guessing which one is missing.

docs.text:
Can Perplexity send or edit a campaign? No. The key carries read scopes and the connector has no send or write tool. Campaigns, flows, and lists are read-only. Why do I get a 403 Forbidden? Over the range you specify, as far back as the Klaviyo account retains the data. Naming a period gives the tightest answer. Does "email revenue" mean the same thing as Shopify revenue? No, and that gap is the usual source of confusion. Klaviyo attributes revenue to the message that drove the session, while Shopify records the order. Asking both connectors the same question is how you see the difference instead of arguing about it. Can it segment by campaign and by flow in one answer? Yes. Campaigns and flows are separate objects, and one question can ask for both and get them split in the reply. Does this work only in Perplexity? No. Klaviyo is exposed to ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity through the same endpoint on the same subscription. Where is the Klaviyo data stored? CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. docs.text:

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:

  4. ChatGPT answers from that result and names the objects each figure came from.

docs.title: Before you connect
docs.text:

  • At least a Viewer role on each ad account - an admin can grant it in Campaign Manager under Account Settings, Manage Access

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. In CorpusIQ, open Dashboard then Connectors and find LinkedIn Ads.
  2. Click Connect.
  3. Sign in to LinkedIn when the consent screen appears.
  4. Approve read access and select the ad accounts you want CorpusIQ to see.
  5. You are returned to CorpusIQ, and the connector turns from gray to green.

In ChatGPT

  1. Install CorpusIQ from the ChatGPT app store, or add the CorpusIQ MCP server under Settings, Connectors.
  2. Approve the CorpusIQ authorization when prompted, once.
  3. Start a new conversation and ask a question that needs your data.

If the connector does not appear, work through the Quick Start guide before changing anything else.

  • "Which creatives are running in my remarketing campaign?"

Accounts

Cross-source

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read-only ad account access. The connector reads memberships, campaigns, creatives and daily analytics.
  • No campaign changes. It never creates campaigns, changes budgets, or modifies ads.

CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Retrieval happens on demand. Operational query logs may persist for up to 30 days. docs.title: How to Connect Mailchimp to Claude with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Email marketing reports answer the easy question. Open rate, click rate, unsubscribes. They do not answer the one the business actually has: did this campaign make money?

That answer lives across Mailchimp and whatever holds the orders. Connecting Mailchimp through CorpusIQ MCP puts the campaign record in the same conversation as the revenue record, so the question can be asked once.

docs.title: Why Connect Mailchimp to Claude?
docs.text:

  • Segment performance. "Which segment has the highest click rate across the last ten campaigns?"
  • Content learning. "What subject lines performed best, and what do the winners have in common?"
  • Churn signals. "Which subscribers stopped opening in the last 60 days?"
  • Read-only by scope. The connection reads campaigns, audiences, and reports. It cannot send, edit, or change a list.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Mailchimp to CorpusIQ with a read-only API key or OAuth, whichever your account supports.
  2. Connect CorpusIQ to Claude as an MCP server, using the config block from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ queries campaigns, reports, audiences, and segments as the question requires.
  4. Claude answers from that retrieved content, with the campaigns it used.

CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. Log in and open Connectors.
  2. Select Mailchimp.
  3. Authorize the connection with a read-only key, or through OAuth if your Mailchimp plan supports it.
  4. Copy the MCP config block shown under Settings, Integrations, Claude Desktop.

In Claude Desktop

  1. Open Settings, Developer, Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Add the CorpusIQ entry:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "corpusiq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Save the file and fully quit Claude Desktop. Not just the window: quit the application.
  2. Reopen Claude, complete the device login when prompted, and the tools indicator appears next to the message box.

If the tools indicator does not appear, work through Claude can't see CorpusIQ before changing anything else.

docs.text:
Can Claude send a campaign through this connection? No. The connection is read-only. Claude reads campaigns, audiences, segments, and reports. Sending, editing, and automation changes are not available. Which Mailchimp plans does this work with? The connector uses Mailchimp's API, which is available across their paid plans. Some reporting detail depends on what your plan exposes, so the answer is limited to the data your account can already show you in the Mailchimp interface. Does it read subscribers, including personal data? It can read audience and segment data, which includes subscriber records. That is why the scope is read-only and revocable, and why the connector should be authorized on an account whose data you are allowed to query. Retrieval is on demand, with no warehouse of subscriber records behind it. Can it compare campaigns with revenue? Yes, once a commerce or billing connector is also connected. "Which campaign drove the most orders last quarter" is one question across Mailchimp and the order system, instead of an export and a manual match. How current is the data? Live. Campaign reports are read at the moment you ask. A send from this morning is visible to the next question, though some Mailchimp metrics settle over the first day. Does it cover automations and journeys? Campaign and audience reporting is the core of this connector. Ask a question that names an automation or a journey and see whether the returned answer is scoped to it. If it is not, the answer will say what it did read rather than guessing. Where is my marketing data stored? CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Retrieval happens on demand. Operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. docs.title: How to Connect Meta Ads to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Meta Ads is where Facebook and Instagram performance lives, and it is one of the hardest platforms to interrogate because the reporting is spread across campaigns, ad sets, audiences, and forms. Connecting Meta Ads to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP gives you a different way in: useful read-only access you authorize once, and then plain-English answers drawn from the live account.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query Facebook and Instagram ad account performance, campaigns, ad sets, individual ads, audience insights, and lead forms, so you can ask about the account instead of navigating it.

docs.title: What you can ask
docs.text:
• "Which campaigns spent the most this month, and what did each return?"
  • "Compare Facebook and Instagram placements by cost per result."
  • "Which ad sets are spending but not producing conversions?"
  • "Which audiences have the highest frequency, and where is fatigue showing?"
  • "How many leads came through our lead forms this quarter, and what did each cost?"
  • "Which creatives have the best cost per result over the last 60 days?"
  • "What is our cost per acquisition trend over the last six months?"

docs.title: What Meta Ads data CorpusIQ reaches
docs.text:

  • Campaigns and ad sets. Performance at the level budget and audience decisions happen.
  • Individual ads. Per-ad results, including creative-level comparison.
  • Audience insights. Who the spend reached and where frequency is climbing.
  • Lead forms. Lead volume and cost from your own forms.

docs.title: Cross-source questions
docs.text:
Paid social is only half the picture, which is exactly where MCP earns its place:

  • "Compare Meta Ads cost per acquisition with Google Ads for the same period."
  • "Do the purchases Meta reports match what our commerce platform booked?"
  • "Which campaigns produced customers with the highest repeat purchase rate?"
  • "Is our Klaviyo email revenue coming from customers we acquired through paid social?"
  • "How does paid social compare with paid search on revenue per dollar spent?"

Each of those needs Meta Ads and another system in the same answer, which is the join MCP provides.

docs.text: CorpusIQ treats Meta as a single connector covering Facebook, Instagram, and Meta Ads, so you authorize once rather than per surface. The scopes required are shown on Meta's own consent screen before you approve.

docs.title: How the connection works
docs.text: You authorize read-only access to the ad account through Meta's OAuth flow, connect the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity, and the assistant calls the Meta retrieval tools when your question needs them. The connection is assistant-agnostic, so the same authorization serves every MCP client you use.

docs.title: Security and data handling
docs.text:
• Read-only. The Meta retrieval tools are marked read-only. The assistant can read and cite ad data, but it cannot change budgets, pause ads, or edit audiences.
  • Bounded, scoped retention. Direct MCP requests fetch live and do not build a raw-file or full-payload warehouse. Scoped operational logs may persist for up to 30 days.
  • Your access controls. Nobody at CorpusIQ can access your accounts, and each user queries under their own authorized credentials.

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Can ChatGPT pause an ad or change a budget?  No. The retrieval tools documented here are marked read-only and provide no execution capability. The assistant analyses and cites your Meta Ads data, but changes stay in Meta Ads Manager.   Does this cover Instagram as well as Facebook?  Yes. Meta is a single CorpusIQ connector covering Facebook, Instagram, and Meta Ads, so placement-level comparison between the two is available in one question.   Can I see lead form performance?  Yes, lead form data is part of the Meta connector, so lead volume and cost per lead are queryable alongside campaign spend.   Is this useful for a small budget as well as a large one?  The cross-source question is useful at any spend level. "Do the purchases Meta reports match what we actually booked?" is worth asking whether you spend hundreds or hundreds of thousands per month.   How current is the data?  CorpusIQ queries Meta through the live API. Meta's own attribution window means recent conversions can still shift for a day or two, which is platform behaviour rather than a CorpusIQ delay.   What access do I need to connect?  You need permission on the ad account that allows authorizing an integration, and the required scopes appear on Meta's consent screen before you approve.

docs.title: How to Connect Monday.com to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Monday.com account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting Monday.com to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live Monday.com data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query your live Monday.com data - workspaces, boards, groups, items (tasks), statuses, owners, and due dates. You ask questions in plain English and get answers from your actual boards in real time.

This page covers the connection architecture, what you can ask, team productivity use cases, security, and how MCP compares to direct Monday.com API integration.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What project management questions can I ask ChatGPT about Monday.com?  Board questions: "What boards do I have access to?", "Show me all items on the Marketing Sprint board." Task questions: "What tasks are assigned to me this week?", "Show me overdue tasks across all boards." Status questions: "How many tasks are in the 'In Progress' stage?", "Which tasks have been in 'Review' for over a week?" Owner questions: "Who has the most open tasks?", "Show me tasks by assignee." Date questions: "What's due this week across all boards?", "Which tasks are past their due date?"  How does the connection work?  CorpusIQ connects to your Monday.com account via OAuth 2.0. You authorize read-only access, then connect the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. ChatGPT discovers the available Monday.com tools - workspace listing, board listing, item retrieval, and column value inspection - and calls them when you ask a question. The MCP server handles the Monday.com GraphQL API, including pagination and column type mapping.  Is the connection read-only?  Yes. CorpusIQ requests read-only external-source retrieval scopes from Monday.com. ChatGPT can see boards, items, statuses, owners, and due dates. It cannot create items, update statuses, reassign tasks, or modify anything in your Monday.com account. The advertised Monday.com retrieval tools are marked read-only; write-capable tools, when available, are separately named and annotated.  What Monday.com data can ChatGPT access?  Workspaces and their metadata. Boards with columns, groups, and structure. Items (tasks/pulses) with column values including status, owner, due date, text, numbers, and dropdown values. The specific columns accessible depend on each board's schema - your custom columns are included.  Can ChatGPT combine Monday.com data with other tools?  Yes. "Show me all Monday.com tasks for HubSpot deals closing this month" combines work management with CRM data. "Which overdue Monday.com tasks are associated with customers who have open support emails in Gmail?" spans work management, CRM, and email. Cross-source context is the hallmark of [MCP platforms like CorpusIQ](benefits-of-mcp-for-business.md).  How is this different from Monday.com's built-in dashboards?  Monday.com's dashboards are pre-configured views with specific widgets. They're excellent for recurring reporting. But they can't answer ad-hoc questions: "Show me tasks that were due last week, are still in progress, and are assigned to people on the engineering team who also have open tasks on the QA board." That's a ChatGPT question - and it would require building a custom dashboard with multiple filters to replicate.  Can I query across multiple boards?  Yes. "Show me all items across all boards assigned to me with a status that's not 'Done'" queries multiple boards simultaneously. "Compare task completion rates across the Engineering and Marketing boards this month" spans boards for comparative analysis.  What about board-level permissions?  CorpusIQ respects Monday.com's board permissions. If you can't see a board in Monday.com, ChatGPT can't see it either. The MCP layer reflects the permission model of the authenticated user.  How does this handle custom columns and complex board schemas?  Monday.com boards can have complex column configurations - status columns, people columns, date columns, formula columns, dependency columns. CorpusIQ's MCP layer maps these into readable formats. Custom columns are accessible by name - just reference them in your question. The MCP server handles the column type detection and value formatting.  Can I use this for daily standup summaries?  Yes. "Give me a standup summary - tasks completed yesterday, tasks planned for today, and any blockers across my boards." One question replaces manually compiling status from multiple Monday.com boards before standup.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Monday.com to CorpusIQ. Dashboard → Connections → Monday.com → sign into Monday.com → authorize read-only access. Takes 2 minutes.

  2. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server. ChatGPT discovers tools for listing workspaces, boards, and items with their column values.

  3. Ask work management questions. ChatGPT maps your question to the appropriate board and item queries, retrieves the data through the MCP server, and returns cited answers.

  4. Iterate with follow-ups. "Now show me just the overdue ones" or "Break that down by assignee" - the conversation builds on previous results.

No Monday.com login required. No board navigation. No manual status compilation.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Instant project visibility. "What's the status of Project X?" replaces navigating to the right board, finding the right group, and mentally compiling status from individual items. One question, one comprehensive answer.

Cross-board insights. "Which projects across all boards are at risk?" queries every board you have access to and identifies items that are overdue or stalled. This cross-board visibility is difficult to achieve within Monday.com's interface.

docs.title: Security: Read-Only by Design
docs.text:
The Monday.com integration is read-only at every layer:

  • OAuth 2.0 with read-only scopes. No write, create, update, or delete permissions.
  • Permission-Respecting. ChatGPT can only see boards and items that the authenticated user has access to in Monday.com.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS 1.3 Encryption. All data in transit is encrypted.

For organizations with sensitive project data, Monday.com remains the authoritative source. CorpusIQ retrieves permitted project data through direct MCP; the retention classes and lifecycles described above still apply.

docs.title: How to Connect Monday.com to Claude with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Monday.com answers "what is the state of the work" only if someone opens the board and reads it. The status someone sets on Tuesday is stale by Thursday, and the groups, columns, and updates that explain why live in a view nobody has open. Connecting Monday.com to Claude through CorpusIQ MCP turns the board into a question you can ask: which items are blocked, who owns what, what slipped this week.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only and does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational query logs are retained for up to 30 days.

docs.title: What Questions Can You Ask?
docs.text:
• "Which items on the Q1 roadmap board are overdue?"
  • "Show me everything assigned to one person this week."
  • "Which projects have been stuck in the same status for more than 14 days?"
  • "Summarize the state of the product board for a Monday standup."
  • "How many items moved to Done last month, by group?"

docs.title: Why Connect Monday.com to Claude?
docs.text:
Boards hold the operational truth: owners, dates, statuses, and the grouping that shows how work is really organized. Reading that truth is manual. Every stakeholder question turns into a filter, a scroll, and a screenshot.

Claude makes the board conversational:

  • Blocked work, surfaced. "Which items are blocked or have no owner?" is one sentence instead of a filter set nobody remembers.
  • Ownership questions answered. "What is on my plate this week?" without exporting a view.
  • Slippage, measured. Compare status movement over time instead of trusting a gut feeling.
  • Cross-source reporting. Put project status beside revenue, spend, or pipeline from other connected tools, in one answer.
  • Briefings on demand. A weekly summary per board, generated from live data rather than a copied dashboard.

docs.title: How the Integration Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Monday.com in CorpusIQ and authorize read access through OAuth.
  2. Add CorpusIQ to Claude as a custom MCP connector. See the Quick Start guide.
  3. Ask. Claude selects the Monday.com tools when a question needs board data, and states which boards and columns it read.
  4. Verify. Every answer is grounded in the live board, so the number matches what you see in Monday.com when you open it.

Read-only is enforced by scope. CorpusIQ never changes statuses, assigns items, edits boards, or creates updates.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
1. Sign up at corpusiq.io. The 30-day trial needs no credit card.
  2. Open Connectors in your CorpusIQ dashboard and select Monday.com.
  3. Click Connect, sign in to Monday.com, and approve the consent screen. The tile changes from gray to green.
  4. Copy the MCP config block shown under Settings, Integrations, Claude Desktop.
  5. Open Claude Desktop, then Settings, Developer, Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json.
  6. Add the CorpusIQ entry:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "corpusiq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Save the file and fully quit Claude Desktop. Not just the window: quit the application.
  2. Reopen Claude and complete the device login when prompted. The tools indicator appears next to the message box.
  3. Verify the data. Ask "Which items are overdue right now?" and check the answer against the board.

If the tools indicator does not appear, work through Claude can't see CorpusIQ before changing anything else.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read-only by scope. The connector requests read access to workspaces, boards, columns, groups, and items. Write-capable tools, where present, are separately named and annotated.
  • No stored payloads. Direct MCP retrieval does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational logs keep query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: Can Claude change item statuses or assign people?  No. The integration is read-only. Claude can read boards and report on them, and it cannot change a status, assign an owner, or edit a board.  Which boards can I read?  The boards your authorizing Monday.com user can see. If a board does not appear, confirm that user has at least view access to it in Monday.com.  Does it read subitems, updates, and column values?  Yes. Board structure, groups, items, and item details including status, owners, dates, and column values are readable. Updates are text and are read as content, not modified.  Can I connect more than one Monday.com account?  Each CorpusIQ user authorizes their own account. Teams that work across more than one workspace typically authorize the account that can see the boards that matter, or use separate users for separate workspaces.  How current is the data?  Every question triggers a fresh read against the live API. There is no nightly sync and no cached copy of your board.

docs.title: How to Connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
SQL Server is where the unglamorous records live: orders, invoices, stock moves, line-of-business tables that an ERP writes and nobody reads without a query window. The data is current and the access is narrow - a handful of people hold the credentials.

Connecting SQL Server through CorpusIQ MCP turns a query request into a question. You ask, the connector runs a SELECT against the database you authorised, and the answer names the tables it read.

CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
tags: connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT

docs.title: Why Connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT?
docs.text:
• Counts without a ticket. "How many customers did we add this quarter?" instead of a request to whoever holds the login.
  • Operational totals. "Show me last month's total sales from the Orders table." Totals, not a CSV.
  • Schema answers. "Describe the schema of the Invoices table" reads back real columns and types.
  • Cross-source questions. A database total checked against the same figure in QuickBooks or Stripe in one pass.
  • Read-only by construction. The connector builds SELECT statements. No INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL.
tags: connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Microsoft SQL Server to CorpusIQ. Enter the host, port, database name and the credentials of a read-only SQL login in the dashboard.
  2. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT as an MCP server, using the endpoint from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ translates the question into read-only queries against your operational record and assembles the result.
  4. ChatGPT answers from that result and names the objects each figure came from.
tags: connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT

docs.title: Before you connect
docs.text:
• Server hostname and port (1433 unless your instance moved it)
  • Database name
  • A SQL login and password - a read-only login is strongly recommended
  • Network reachability: if the server sits on a private network, allowlist the outbound address shown in your dashboard
tags: connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. Open your CorpusIQ dashboard and go to Connectors.
  2. Find Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL) and click Connect. This is a direct configuration form, not an OAuth flow.
  3. Enter the host, port, database name, username and password.
  4. Optionally toggle encryption and certificate trust so they match your server's setup.
  5. Save. The connector turns from gray to green once the first connection succeeds.

In ChatGPT

  1. Install CorpusIQ from the ChatGPT app store, or add the CorpusIQ MCP server under Settings, Connectors.
  2. Approve the CorpusIQ authorization when prompted, once.
  3. Start a new conversation and ask a question that needs your data.

If the connector does not appear, work through the Quick Start guide before changing anything else.
tags: connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT

docs.title: Example ChatGPT Questions
docs.text:
Inventory and structure

  • "List the tables in the warehouse database."
  • "Describe the schema of the Invoices table, including column types."
  • "Which tables look transactional rather than reference data?"

Revenue and customers

  • "Show me last month's total sales from the Orders table."
  • "How many customers did we add this quarter?"
  • "Which customers ordered more than 10,000 in the last 90 days?"

Cross-source

  • "Does the Orders table total for last month match the QuickBooks revenue figure?" (requires the QuickBooks connector)
  • "Which customers in the CRM have no rows in the Orders table?" (requires the CRM connector)
tags: connect Microsoft SQL Server to ChatGPT

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read-only login. Create a SQL login that holds SELECT on the schemas you want exposed, and nothing else. That grant is the boundary.
  • SELECT only. The connector builds SELECT statements. It does not insert, update, delete, or run schema changes.
  • Network position. A private instance stays private until its firewall allows the connection, so an allowlist sits in front of the credential.
  • Revocable at any time. Disable the SQL login or remove the connection in CorpusIQ and access stops.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.text: Question The native interface CorpusIQ MCP with ChatGPT Input A query window and knowledge of the schema A question in plain language Output Rows you read A synthesised answer naming the tables used Access Whoever holds the login The read-only login you scoped Write path Whatever the login allows None exposed to the assistant Cross-source Copy the result into another tool Asked alongside finance and CRM data

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Does this work with Azure SQL as well as SQL Server? Yes. Azure SQL is the same engine reached over the network, so the same host, port, database and credential fields apply. Add the outbound address to the server's firewall rules. Do I have to use a read-only login? The connector only ever builds SELECT statements, but a read-only login means a mistake upstream cannot become a write. Create the login with SELECT on the schemas you want answerable and leave it there. Login failed. What should I check? SQL Authentication has to be enabled on the server - Windows Authentication alone is not enough for this connection type. Then confirm the username, password and database name. Cannot open server. Is the password wrong? Usually not. That error is the network: the server's firewall is refusing the connection. Allowlist the outbound address shown in your CorpusIQ dashboard. Encryption error on save. What now? A self-signed certificate fails the default trust check. Toggle "Trust server certificate" to match your server's setup, or install a certificate the server can validate. Which tables can the assistant see? Exactly the tables your SQL login can read. If a table is missing from answers, the login is missing the grant - that is the intended control point.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Does this work with Azure SQL as well as SQL Server? Yes. Azure SQL is the same engine reached over the network, so the same host, port, database and credential fields apply. Add the outbound address to the server's firewall rules. Do I have to use a read-only login? The connector only ever builds SELECT statements, but a read-only login means a mistake upstream cannot become a write. Create the login with SELECT on the schemas you want answerable and leave it there. Login failed. What should I check? SQL Authentication has to be enabled on the server - Windows Authentication alone is not enough for this connection type. Then confirm the username, password and database name. Cannot open server. Is the password wrong? Usually not. That error is the network: the server's firewall is refusing the connection. Allowlist the outbound address shown in your CorpusIQ dashboard. Encryption error on save. What now? A self-signed certificate fails the default trust check. Toggle "Trust server certificate" to match your server's setup, or install a certificate the server can validate. Which tables can the assistant see? Exactly the tables your SQL login can read. If a table is missing from answers, the login is missing the grant - that is the intended control point.

docs.title: How to Connect NetSuite to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your NetSuite account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting NetSuite to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live NetSuite data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query your live NetSuite data - financial reports, sales orders, customer records, inventory levels, and project status. You ask questions in plain English and get answers from your live ERP, without touching the NetSuite UI or writing a single line of SuiteScript.

This page covers the architecture, what you can ask, enterprise security, and how MCP compares to direct NetSuite API integration and SuiteScript development.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What NetSuite data can ChatGPT access?  CorpusIQ's NetSuite integration provides access to core ERP objects: sales orders, customers, invoices, inventory, items, financial reports, and project data. ChatGPT can retrieve individual records, list records with filters, and aggregate data across objects. NetSuite connector retrieval is read-only - no record creation, editing, or deletion in that source.  What questions can I ask ChatGPT about NetSuite?  Financial questions: "What's our P&L by subsidiary this month?", "Show me open invoices by aging bucket." Order questions: "What sales orders are scheduled to ship this week?", "Show me orders on hold." Customer questions: "Who are our top 20 customers by revenue YTD?", "Which customers haven't ordered in 90 days?" Inventory questions: "What items are below reorder point?", "Show me inventory by warehouse." Project questions: "What's the status of active projects?", "Which projects are over budget?"  How does CorpusIQ connect NetSuite to ChatGPT?  CorpusIQ connects to NetSuite using token-based authentication (TBA) - the enterprise-standard method for NetSuite API access. You create an integration record, generate access tokens with read-only permissions, and configure the connection in CorpusIQ. Once connected, the CorpusIQ MCP server exposes NetSuite data as tools that ChatGPT can call. The MCP server handles SuiteTalk/SOAP web services, RESTlet calls, or SuiteQL queries behind the scenes.  Is the connection read-only?  Yes. The NetSuite integration uses token-based authentication with a role that has read-only permissions. ChatGPT can query records, run saved searches, and retrieve reports. It cannot create, edit, or delete any NetSuite records. The read-only guarantee is enforced by the NetSuite role permissions assigned to the integration.  How does this handle NetSuite's complexity - subsidiaries, custom fields, workflows?  NetSuite is highly customizable, and CorpusIQ's MCP layer is designed to work with that complexity. Custom fields are accessible - just reference them in your question. Subsidiary data can be queried per-subsidiary or consolidated. Saved searches can be referenced by name. The MCP layer adapts to your NetSuite configuration, not the other way around.  Can ChatGPT combine NetSuite data with other tools?  Yes - cross-source queries are where MCP delivers the most value. "Does this month's NetSuite revenue match our Stripe processing volume?" "Show me NetSuite customers who have open HubSpot deals." "Which NetSuite inventory items have corresponding Shopify listings that are out of stock?" These multi-system questions combine your ERP with your CRM, ecommerce, and payment platforms in one ChatGPT response.  How is this different from NetSuite's built-in reporting?  NetSuite's reporting tools - saved searches, reports, SuiteAnalytics - are powerful and essential for formal financial reporting. But they require NetSuite expertise to build and maintain. ChatGPT with MCP provides ad-hoc access: questions that don't fit into a pre-built saved search but matter for daily operations. It's a complement to NetSuite's reporting, not a replacement.  What about SuiteScript - do I still need it?  SuiteScript remains essential for custom business logic, automation, and integrations that require write operations or complex workflows. But for data access - the most common reason people write SuiteScript - ChatGPT with MCP eliminates the need. Instead of writing a script to pull customer order history, you ask "Show me order history for Customer X" and get the answer immediately.  What permissions do I need in NetSuite?  You need a NetSuite account with permissions to create an integration record and generate access tokens. The integration role should have read-only access to the record types you want to query. A NetSuite administrator typically handles this setup, which takes about 5-10 minutes one time.  How does this handle multi-subsidiary NetSuite instances?  CorpusIQ can query across subsidiaries. Specify the subsidiary in your question ("Show me Q2 revenue for the EMEA subsidiary") or ask for consolidated views ("Show me consolidated revenue across all subsidiaries this quarter"). The MCP layer handles subsidiary context transparently.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Set up NetSuite integration. In NetSuite, create an integration record, assign a read-only role, and generate consumer key/secret and token ID/secret. This is a one-time setup by your NetSuite admin.

  2. Connect NetSuite to CorpusIQ. In your CorpusIQ dashboard, click Connections → NetSuite → enter your account ID and token credentials. CorpusIQ validates the connection and confirms available record types.

  3. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server. ChatGPT discovers available ERP tools for financials, orders, customers, inventory, and more.

  4. Ask ERP questions. ChatGPT maps your natural language question to the appropriate NetSuite records, executes the query through the MCP server, and returns a cited answer.

  5. Combine with other data. Ask questions that span NetSuite and your other connected tools - CRM, ecommerce, payment platforms, and analytics.

No SuiteScript. No saved searches to build. No CSV exports to analyze in Excel.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
ERP data democratization. Your sales team, operations team, and executives can get NetSuite answers without NetSuite licenses or training. Natural language is the only interface required.

Faster operational decisions. "Do we have enough inventory to fulfill this week's open orders?" - a question that could require checking three NetSuite screens - becomes one ChatGPT query.

Cross-department visibility. "Show me NetSuite customers with open opportunities in HubSpot" combines ERP and CRM data. "Match NetSuite revenue against Stripe payouts" combines ERP and payment data. Only MCP platforms like CorpusIQ provide this cross-source context.

Reduced SuiteScript dependency. Every ad-hoc data question that would normally require a custom SuiteScript becomes a ChatGPT conversation. Free your NetSuite developers for higher-value work.

Enterprise governance. Read-only by role design with an audit trail. Direct MCP avoids a raw-file/full-payload warehouse; scoped operational logs may persist for up to 30 days.

"Which HubSpot deals closed this month don't have corresponding NetSuite sales orders?" These reconciliation questions catch discrepancies that would otherwise surface at month-end close.

docs.title: Security: Enterprise ERP Security
docs.text:
The NetSuite integration's security model is enforced by NetSuite's own permission system:

  • Token-Based Authentication (TBA). Industry-standard NetSuite API authentication. No passwords, no session cookies.
  • Role-Based Permissions. The NetSuite role assigned to the integration determines exactly which records and fields are accessible. Create a read-only role and grant only the record types you need.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS 1.3 Encryption. All data in transit is encrypted.
  • Audit Trail. NetSuite's built-in audit trail logs all API access, providing visibility into exactly what data was queried and when.

For enterprises with strict compliance requirements, NetSuite remains the authoritative source. CorpusIQ retrieves permitted ERP records through direct MCP; the retention classes and lifecycles described above still apply.

docs.title: How to Connect NetSuite to Perplexity with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Perplexity is good at the world outside the ERP: supply chain news, freight rates, the announcement from a vendor you depend on.

It cannot see your inventory position, your open purchase orders, or your P&L by subsidiary, because none of that is public.

Connecting NetSuite through CorpusIQ MCP puts both in one thread. Perplexity answers the ERP question from your own account, read-only, and names the records it read.

docs.title: Why Connect NetSuite to Perplexity?
docs.text:
• Margin in context. "Our gross margin by subsidiary for the quarter is on screen. What moved in our input costs this quarter?" Both halves answered in one thread.
  • Inventory versus demand. "Which SKUs are below their reorder point, and which of those suppliers had lead time warnings this month?"
  • Procurement. "Which purchase orders are open past their expected delivery date, by vendor?"
  • Subsidiary consolidation. Ask across entities without a saved search for each one.
  • Order to cash. "What is our order to cash cycle by subsidiary?" instead of a workbook built by hand.
  • Read-only by role. Token-based authentication with a read-only role. The retrieval tools documented on this page are read-only.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Create a read-only integration role in NetSuite and generate token-based authentication tokens.
  2. Connect NetSuite to CorpusIQ with the account ID, consumer key, consumer secret, token ID and token secret.
  3. Add CorpusIQ to Perplexity as a custom remote MCP server, using the endpoint from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  4. CorpusIQ reads the records that answer the question through the SuiteTalk REST API.
  5. Perplexity answers from that result, with the surrounding market context you asked for.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs keep query text, per-user tool-call metadata and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In NetSuite

  1. Ask a NetSuite administrator to create an integration record for CorpusIQ.
  2. Build a role that carries read permissions only, on the record types you want answerable.
  3. Generate the token-based authentication credentials for that role: consumer key, consumer secret, token ID and token secret.

In CorpusIQ

  1. Open your dashboard and go to Connectors.
  2. Select NetSuite and enter the Account ID, Consumer Key, Consumer Secret, Token ID and Token Secret.
  3. Choose which record types are reachable. The connector turns green.

In Perplexity

  1. Open Settings and find the MCP servers section.
  2. Add a custom MCP server and paste the endpoint:
https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp
  1. Connect and approve the CorpusIQ authorization page once.
  2. Start a new thread and ask a question about your ERP data.

The setup is a one-time token entry with a NetSuite admin. There is no SuiteScript to write and no saved search to maintain.

docs.text:
• Read-only role. A dedicated NetSuite role limited to read permissions decides what the connector can reach. It never sees a record type you did not grant.

docs.text:
Can Perplexity change anything in NetSuite? No. The retrieval tools documented on this page are read-only, and the integration role carries read permissions. Transactions, inventory and vendor records are untouched. Does this cover multi-currency and multi-subsidiary accounts? Yes. Transactions return at line level with their original currencies, and answers can be scoped to a subsidiary or asked across all of them. Which NetSuite API does the connector use? The SuiteTalk REST API with token-based authentication. OneWorld accounts consolidate through the same path. How current is the data? Live. Each question reads the current state of the account, so a receipt posted this morning appears in the next answer. Verify time-sensitive figures against the cited record. Does this work only in Perplexity? No. NetSuite is exposed to ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity through the same endpoint on the same subscription. What happens when the tokens rotate? Rotate the tokens in NetSuite and re-enter them in CorpusIQ. Questions stop working until the new credentials are in, so keep the rotation on a known schedule. Where is the NetSuite data stored? CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. docs.title: How to Connect Notion to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Your Notion account holds critical business data - but accessing insights usually means logging in, navigating dashboards, and running manual reports. Connecting Notion to ChatGPT through CorpusIQ MCP eliminates all that friction. Once connected via a secure OAuth flow, ChatGPT can query your live Notion data directly - you ask questions in plain English, and get cited answers drawn from your actual account, not outdated exports or screenshots.

Once connected, ChatGPT can query your live Notion workspace - pages, databases, blocks, and users. You ask questions in plain English and get cited answers from your actual Notion content in real time. Your company wiki becomes a conversational knowledge base.

This page covers the connection architecture, what you can ask, knowledge management use cases, security, and how MCP compares to Notion's built-in search and API.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: What knowledge base questions can I ask ChatGPT about Notion?  Page questions: "What's in our employee onboarding guide?", "Show me the Q3 product roadmap page", "What does our pricing page say about enterprise plans?" Database questions: "Show me all active projects from the Project Tracker database", "What tasks are assigned to me in the Sprint database?", "List all candidates in the Hiring Pipeline database." Cross-page questions: "What's our company policy on remote work?", "Find all pages that mention the API migration", "Summarize what our documentation says about security compliance." Workspace questions: "What databases do we have?", "Show me recently updated pages", "Who are the workspace members?"  How does the connection work?  CorpusIQ connects to your Notion workspace via an Internal Integration Token. You create the integration in Notion, grant it read access to specific pages or the entire workspace, then paste the token into CorpusIQ. Once connected, add the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. ChatGPT discovers tools for searching pages, querying databases, reading page content, and listing workspace users. The MCP server handles Notion's API, including block traversal, database queries, and pagination.  Is the connection read-only?  Yes. The Notion integration token is configured with read-only capabilities. ChatGPT can search pages, query databases, and read block content. It cannot create pages, edit content, modify databases, or change anything in your Notion workspace. The read-only guarantee is enforced by the integration token's capabilities in Notion.  What Notion content can ChatGPT access?  Pages with titles, properties, and content blocks (paragraphs, headings, lists, toggles, callouts). Databases with schema, properties, and row data. Page content through block traversal - ChatGPT can read the actual text of your pages, not just metadata. The specific content accessible depends on which pages you've shared with the integration - you control exactly what's accessible.  Can ChatGPT search across all Notion pages at once?  Yes. "Search Notion for everything about the Q4 product launch" searches across all pages the integration has access to. "Find all mentions of 'security review' across our documentation" spans the entire integrated workspace. This is significantly more powerful than Notion's built-in search, which returns page titles and snippets - ChatGPT reads full page content and synthesizes answers.  How is this different from Notion's built-in AI features?  Notion AI (Notion's built-in AI assistant) is designed for content creation within Notion - writing, summarizing, translating, and editing Notion pages. It works within a single page context. ChatGPT connected via MCP provides cross-page knowledge retrieval: "What does our entire documentation say about the authentication flow?" queries every relevant page and synthesizes an answer. ChatGPT also connects Notion knowledge with data from your other tools - CRM, project management, analytics - providing business context that isolated Notion AI cannot.  Can ChatGPT query Notion databases with filters?  Yes. "Show me all tasks in the Engineering Sprint database where Status is 'In Progress' and Priority is 'High'" works naturally. "List all candidates in the Hiring Pipeline who are in the 'Final Interview' stage." Database queries with property filters work through natural language - no need to build Notion database views or filter configurations.  What about access control - can ChatGPT see private pages?  ChatGPT can only access pages that have been explicitly shared with the Notion integration. If a page isn't shared with the integration, ChatGPT can't see it - even if the authorizing user can. This is a Notion API design constraint that actually provides stronger access control: you must explicitly grant the integration access to each top-level page or database, providing fine-grained control over what ChatGPT can query.  How does this handle large Notion workspaces with thousands of pages?  ChatGPT can search across the workspace efficiently. "Search for pages about the rebranding project" narrows results to relevant content. For database queries, filtering reduces result sets. "Show me the 10 most recently updated pages" provides a quick workspace overview. The search-first approach means ChatGPT finds relevant content without needing to read every page.  Can ChatGPT extract structured data from Notion databases?  Yes. Notion databases are structured collections with typed properties - text, select, multi-select, date, number, person, formula. ChatGPT can query these with property filters and return structured results. "Show me all projects with a deadline this month, sorted by priority" returns structured project data from your Notion project database.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Create a Notion integration. In Notion, go to Settings → Integrations → Create new integration. Give it a name and select read-only capabilities. Copy the integration token.

  2. Share pages with the integration. In Notion, for each top-level page or database you want ChatGPT to access, click Share → invite your integration.

  3. Connect Notion to CorpusIQ. Dashboard → Connections → Notion → paste your integration token. CorpusIQ validates the token and confirms connected pages.

  4. Connect CorpusIQ to ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server. ChatGPT discovers tools for searching, reading pages, querying databases, and listing users.

  5. Ask knowledge questions. ChatGPT searches your Notion workspace, reads relevant pages, and returns cited answers with page references.

No manual page navigation. No database filter building. Knowledge retrieval becomes conversational.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Conversational knowledge retrieval. Instead of searching Notion for keywords and clicking through pages, ask "What's our refund policy?" or "How do we handle PTO requests?" and get the answer synthesized from your actual documentation. Your company wiki becomes a conversational knowledge base.

Cross-document synthesis. "Summarize everything our documentation says about the API authentication flow" reads across multiple pages and databases and produces a unified answer. This cross-document synthesis is something Notion's built-in search cannot do.

Database-powered Q&A. "Show me all active projects with a deadline this quarter" or "List all open positions with their hiring manager" - your Notion databases become queryable by natural language, not just by building database views.

Business-connected knowledge. "Show me the project brief for the HubSpot deal with Acme Corp" or "What's our documentation say about the integration that the Stripe team is asking about?" Notion knowledge connected to CRM and payment data provides richer context than isolated documentation. This cross-source capability is unique to MCP platforms like CorpusIQ.

Accelerated onboarding. New hires can ask ChatGPT about company policies, project documentation, and team processes - getting answers from Notion without knowing which pages to look at or how the workspace is organized.

docs.text: "What's our travel policy?" "How do I set up my development environment?" "What's the process for submitting an expense report?" Company policies and procedures become instantly answerable.

"Find Notion documentation about the payment flow and cross-reference with Stripe transaction data." Combining documentation with live business data provides complete context.

docs.title: Security: Read-Only with Fine-Grained Access Control
docs.text:
The Notion integration provides layered security:

  • Integration Token with read-only capabilities. No content creation, editing, or deletion.
  • Page-Level Sharing. You explicitly share each top-level page and database with the integration. Unshared pages are inaccessible regardless of workspace membership.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. Notion retrieval tools are marked read-only. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS 1.3 Encryption. All data in transit is encrypted.
  • Provider authorization. Manage the integration token through Notion; provider-side timing remains governed by Notion.

For organizations with sensitive documentation - IP, strategy, customer data - this architecture provides granular access control: expose only the pages you want ChatGPT to access, and manage provider authorization in Notion when needed.

docs.title: How to Connect Notion to Perplexity with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Perplexity is strong on the public record: industry practice, regulation, what the standard approach looks like elsewhere.

What it cannot tell you is what your own company decided. The onboarding guide, the pricing policy, the sprint board, the hiring pipeline and the process nobody wrote down outside Notion are all invisible to it.

Connecting Notion through CorpusIQ MCP puts those two halves in one thread. Perplexity answers from your own workspace, read-only, and cites the page or database it read.

docs.title: Why Connect Notion to Perplexity?
docs.text:
• Policy with the outside view. "What does our remote work policy say, and how does it compare to what comparable companies publish?"
  • Process answers. "What is our documented process for approving a discount above 20 percent?"
  • Project state. "Which projects in the tracker are behind their target date, and who owns each?"
  • Hiring pipeline. "How many candidates are in final interview this month, at the stage we usually lose them?"
  • Documentation coverage. "Which of our product pages have not been updated since the last release?"
  • Read-only by capability. The retrieval tools documented on this page are read-only, and the integration token is created with read content access.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Create a Notion internal integration, grant it read content capability, and share the pages or databases you want reachable.
  2. Connect Notion to CorpusIQ by pasting the integration token.
  3. Add CorpusIQ to Perplexity as a custom remote MCP server, using the endpoint from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  4. Perplexity answers from the pages and database rows the integration can see, and names the page it read.

Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs keep query text, per-user tool-call metadata and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In Notion

  1. Open Settings and members, then Integrations, and create a new internal integration.
  2. Set its capabilities to read content. Do not enable insert or update.
  3. Copy the integration token.
  4. Open each page or database you want reachable, choose Connections, and add the integration. Notion requires explicit sharing per page.

In CorpusIQ

  1. Open your dashboard and go to Connectors.
  2. Select Notion and paste the integration token. The connector turns green.

In Perplexity

  1. Open Settings and find the MCP servers section.
  2. Add a custom MCP server and paste the endpoint:
https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp
  1. Connect and approve the CorpusIQ authorization page once.
  2. Start a new thread and ask about a page or a database.

Sharing is the real access boundary. A page that is not shared with the integration cannot be read, even by a workspace owner.

docs.title: Example Perplexity Questions
docs.text:
Policy and knowledge

  • "What does our onboarding guide say, and what does comparable practice look like for a company our size?"
  • "Summarize our security policy, then tell me which framework clauses it leaves unaddressed."
  • "What did we decide about remote work, and how common is that policy in our industry?"

Databases and trackers

  • "List every project in the tracker with status In Progress and a target date this quarter."
  • "Which candidates in the hiring pipeline have been in final interview for more than two weeks?"
  • "What changed in the pricing database this month, and who changed it?"

Documentation health

  • "Which pages have not been updated since the last product release?"
  • "Find every page that mentions the API migration and summarize how they differ."
  • "Which product pages contradict each other on pricing?"

Cross-source

  • "Do the projects marked done in Notion match the epics closed in Jira?" (requires the Jira connector)
  • "Which accounts mentioned in the CRM also have a Notion page, and does the status agree?" (requires a CRM connector)
  • "Compare the hiring plan in Notion with the headcount figures in the finance system." (requires a finance connector)

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Read-only retrieval tools. The tools documented on this page are read-only, and the integration is created with read content capability only.
  • Explicit sharing per page. Notion requires you to share each page or database with the integration, so the reachable set is the set you chose.
  • No stored credentials on your side. CorpusIQ holds the encrypted token; you can revoke it in Notion at any time, and revocation takes effect on the next call.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. Raw customer files and full connector payloads are not retained. Operational logs keep query text, tool-call metadata and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.
  • TLS in transit between Notion, CorpusIQ and Perplexity.

docs.title: Comparison: Notion Search and Notion AI vs Notion in Perplexity
docs.text:
Aspect Notion search and Notion AI CorpusIQ MCP with Perplexity Input A phrase, or a question inside one page A question across the pages you shared Scope Titles, snippets, one page context Full page content and database rows Outside context Open a second tab Same thread, same answer Cross-system Copy content out by hand Asked across connectors Synthesis Page-level Across pages and databases Write access Yes, by your users None through the retrieval tools

Notion search finds the page. A connected workspace answers the question that spans five of them.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Can Perplexity edit or create Notion pages? No. The integration is created with read content capability and the retrieval tools documented on this page are read-only. Content, databases and settings are untouched. Does it see every page in the workspace? Only the pages and databases you shared with the integration. That is a stronger boundary than a workspace-wide token: nothing outside the shared set is reachable. Can it query database properties and filters? Yes. Notion databases carry typed properties such as select, date, number and person, and a question can filter on them: "every project with status In Progress and priority High". Does it read page content or only titles? Full content through block traversal, including paragraphs, headings, lists and callouts, plus database schema and rows. How current is the data? Live. Each question reads the current state of the pages you shared, so an edit made a minute ago appears in the next answer. Does this work only in Perplexity? No. Notion is exposed to ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity through the same endpoint on the same subscription. Where is the Notion data stored? CorpusIQ does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Operational logs may persist for up to 30 days. See the [read-only and security documentation](/hermes/security/read-only-and-security).

docs.title: How to Connect Odoo to ChatGPT with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Odoo is many applications sharing one database. The value is in the joins: a quotation that became an invoice, an invoice against a delivery, a delivery against stock on hand. The interface makes you open four screens and join them yourself.

Connecting Odoo through CorpusIQ MCP makes those cross-module questions answerable inside ChatGPT, read-only, with the module and record named in the answer.

docs.title: What Questions Can You Ask?
docs.text:
Sales and pipeline

  • "What is the value of open quotations in Odoo right now?"
  • "How many opportunities are in the negotiation stage?"
  • "Which sales orders are confirmed but not yet delivered?"

Money owed

  • "Show me overdue customer invoices."
  • "What is the total of vendor bills due in the next 14 days?"
  • "Which customers have both an overdue invoice and an open quotation?"

Inventory

  • "What is on hand for SKU X across all warehouses?"
  • "Which products are below their reorder point?"

Operations

  • "List active projects and their task counts."
  • "Which project tasks are past their deadline?"

Cross-source

  • "Compare Odoo invoiced revenue against Stripe payouts this month." (requires the Stripe connector)
  • "Which Odoo customers also have open deals in HubSpot?" (requires the HubSpot connector)

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text: Can ChatGPT confirm orders, post invoices or move stock?  No. Every exposed tool is a read: partners, sale orders and quotations with line items, CRM leads and opportunities, customer and vendor invoices, products and on-hand inventory, stock transfers, journals, payments, taxes, employees, projects and tasks.  What do I need to connect Odoo?  Your Odoo instance URL, the database name, a login, and an API key for a user with read access to the modules you want visible. Setup takes about three minutes.  Does this work with Odoo Online, Odoo.sh and self-hosted?  Yes. Any instance that answers over HTTPS with a reachable database name works, including Odoo Online, Odoo.sh and a self-hosted deployment.  Authentication failed. What should I check?  Generate a fresh API key in Odoo under Preferences, then Account Security, and reconnect. A key created for a different user will also fail if that user lacks module access.  One module comes back empty.  The connected user probably has no access rights to that module's records. Odoo enforces its own permissions, so the connection can only read what the user can open in the interface.  What is retained after a query?  Direct MCP retrieval is read-only. Raw customer files and full connector response payloads are not retained; operational query logs keep query text and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. You enter your instance URL, database name, login and API key in the CorpusIQ connector form and save.
  2. CorpusIQ verifies the credentials against the instance and exposes the readable modules as read-only MCP tools.
  3. You add the CorpusIQ MCP server to ChatGPT. See the Quick Start guide.
  4. ChatGPT calls the module the question needs and joins the records it returns.
  5. The answer names the module and the period, so the figure can be reconciled in Odoo.

  2. Connect Odoo. Open Dashboard, then Connections, find Odoo, then enter your instance URL, the database name, a login and an API key with read access.
  3. Connect ChatGPT. Add the CorpusIQ MCP server per the Quick Start guide.
  4. Verify. Ask "how many opportunities are in each stage". Real stage names mean the connection is live.
  5. Explore. Then ask the cross-module question that has meant four screens and a manual join.

docs.title: How to Connect Odoo to Claude with CorpusIQ MCP
docs.text:
Odoo holds the operating record: quotations, invoices, inventory, projects, employees. It also spreads that record across modules, so a question that crosses modules becomes a tour of the menu.

Connecting Odoo to Claude through CorpusIQ MCP collapses that tour. Ask what open quotations are worth and which customers owe you money, and both answers arrive with the records behind them.

docs.title: Why Connect Odoo to Claude?
docs.text:
• Cross-module questions. Sales, invoicing, inventory and projects answered in one response instead of four screens.
  • Quotation and order visibility. Open quotations, their line items and their total value, without building a filter.
  • Receivables. Overdue customer invoices and vendor bills read as a list.
  • Stock position. On-hand quantities per product and location, asked as a sentence.
  • Project and people context. Active projects, task counts and employee records read alongside the commercial data.
  • No write path. The connection reads records. It never confirms orders, posts invoices or moves stock.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Connect Odoo to CorpusIQ with your instance URL, database name, login and API key.
  2. Connect CorpusIQ to Claude as an MCP server, using the config block from your CorpusIQ account settings.
  3. CorpusIQ translates your question into Odoo record reads across the modules involved, then assembles the results.
  4. Claude answers from those records and names the module and record type each figure comes from.

CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Setup Steps
docs.text:
In CorpusIQ

  1. Log in to CorpusIQ and open Connectors.
  2. Select Odoo and click Connect.
  3. Enter your Odoo URL, for example https://yourcompany.odoo.com, the database name shown on the Odoo login screen, your login and an API key.
  4. Save. CorpusIQ verifies the connection and Odoo turns from gray to green.
  5. Copy the MCP config block under Settings, Integrations, Claude Desktop.

In Claude Desktop

  1. Open Settings, Developer, Edit Config. This opens claude_desktop_config.json.
  2. Add the CorpusIQ entry:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "corpusiq": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y", "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
  1. Save the file and fully quit Claude Desktop. Not just the window: quit the application.
  2. Reopen Claude, complete the device login when prompted, and the tools indicator appears next to the message box.

If the tools indicator does not appear, work through Claude can't see CorpusIQ before changing anything else.

docs.text:
Sales and pipeline questions

  • "Show me sale orders confirmed this week with their totals."

Finance questions

  • "Show me overdue customer invoices."
  • "Which vendor bills are unpaid?"
  • "What did we invoice last month, by customer?"
  • "How much tax did we collect last quarter?"

Inventory and project questions

  • "Which products are below their reorder point?"
  • "List active projects and their task counts."

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Record-level access. Odoo enforces the connected user's access rights, so Claude sees the modules and records that user can already open. Connect a read-scoped user if you want the boundary explicit.
  • No write path. CorpusIQ reads records. There is no confirm, post, validate or stock-move path exposed to the assistant.
  • Revocable at any time. Revoke the API key in Odoo under Preferences, Account Security, and the connection stops working.
  • Scoped direct-MCP retention. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days.

docs.text:
Question Odoo UI CorpusIQ MCP with Claude Input Module, menu, filters A question in plain language Output Record lists you read A synthesized answer with records named Cross-module One module at a time Sales, finance and stock in one answer Exports Manual list export Structured text on request Write access Full record access in the UI None exposed to the assistant

Odoo records the business. Claude answers questions about it without making anyone learn the menu structure.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Does this work with Odoo Online, Odoo.sh and self-hosted instances? Yes. The connection takes your instance URL, database name, login and API key, which covers Odoo Online, Odoo.sh and self-hosted deployments. Can Claude confirm orders or post invoices? No. The connection reads records only. Order confirmation, invoice posting and stock moves stay in Odoo, performed by your team. What happens if a module looks empty? Generate the API key from that user's Preferences, Account Security page. The key inherits that user's access rights. Authentication failed. What should I check? Generate a fresh API key in Odoo and confirm the database name matches exactly what the Odoo login screen shows. How current is the data? Each question runs against your Odoo instance when you ask, so records created this morning are included.

docs.title: FAQ: Common Questions
docs.text:
Can Perplexity confirm an order or post an invoice in Odoo? No. The connection carries read access and the connector has no write tool. Orders, invoices, stock, and partners are untouched. Why does it say the database was not found? The database name must match exactly what Odoo shows on the login screen, including any suffix. A near match is a different database. Why is a module empty in the answers? The connected Odoo user lacks access rights to that module's records. Grant read access to that user, or connect with a user who already has it.
