Connectors used: HubSpot or LeadConnector, Email, Calendar, QuickBooks, Shopify. Behind the scenes: crm-pipeline-health skill. Sample answer shape: Stage-by-stage pipeline health with stalled-deal list and forecast confidence note.

docs.title: "Which deals are stuck?"
docs.text: What this does: Ranks open deals by days-since-last-activity. Surfaces ones with no email/calendar touch. Connectors used: HubSpot, Email, Calendar. Behind the scenes: crm-pipeline-health. Sample answer shape: Deal list with amount, stage, days idle, last contact.

docs.title: "Score every customer by health."
docs.text: What this does: Account-by-account health scoring - usage, billing, engagement, support signals. Identifies healthy / at-risk / critical. Connectors used: HubSpot, GA4 (or PostHog), Email, QuickBooks. Behind the scenes: customer-health-scorecard skill. Sample answer shape: Ranked list with health score, top driver, and recommended action per account.

docs.title: "Which customers are about to churn?"
docs.text: What this does: Surfaces at-risk accounts before cancellation - declining engagement, failed payments, support escalations. Connectors used: HubSpot, Email, QuickBooks, Klaviyo (if available). Behind the scenes: churn-prevention skill. Sample answer shape: At-risk account list with risk signals and a suggested save play.

docs.title: "Find the contact record for Jane at Acme."
docs.text: What this does: Searches your CRM for a person. Connectors used: HubSpot or LeadConnector. Behind the scenes: search_hubspot_contacts or search_leadconnector_contacts. Sample answer shape: Matching contacts with email, phone, company, and last-activity.

docs.title: "Prep me for my call with Acme."
docs.text: What this does: Pulls everything CorpusIQ has on a specific account - CRM deal, recent emails, past meetings, invoice/payment history, support threads. Connectors used: HubSpot, Email, Calendar, QuickBooks. Behind the scenes: sales-call-prep-brief skill. Sample answer shape: A pre-call brief - relationship state, open items, last touchpoint, suggested talking points.

docs.title: "Prepare a QBR deck for [customer name]."
docs.text: What this does: Builds a quarterly business review brief - usage metrics, wins, open issues, expansion angles. Connectors used: HubSpot, GA4 or PostHog, Email. Behind the scenes: qbr-prep-assembler skill. Sample answer shape: Structured QBR sections populated from the account's actuals.

docs.title: "How are bookings going? What's the meeting-to-close rate?"
docs.text: What this does: Analyzes the booked-meeting funnel - bookings, no-shows, demos completed, demo-to-deal rate. Connectors used: Calendly, HubSpot, Calendar. Behind the scenes: meeting-funnel-analyst skill. Sample answer shape: Funnel from booked → showed → converted with conversion rate per stage.

docs.title: "List my most engaged customer contacts this month."
docs.text:
What this does: Cross-references CRM with email and calendar activity. Connectors used: HubSpot, Email, Calendar. Behind the scenes: Pipeline + engagement join. Sample answer shape: Contact list ranked by touchpoint count.

docs.title: Data Analysis Prompts - SQL, Reporting & Visualization
First-Look Analysis
docs.text:
You are a data analyst. I'm sharing a dataset with [N] rows and [M] columns from [SOURCE SYSTEM].

Schema:
[PASTE COLUMN NAMES AND TYPES]

Answer these discovery questions:
1. What are the top 5 most frequent values in [COLUMN]?
2. What time range does [DATE COLUMN] span?
3. Which columns have the most missing/null values?
4. Are there any obvious outliers in [NUMERIC COLUMNS]?
5. What correlations exist between [COLUMN A] and [COLUMN B]?

Summarize in plain English what the data represents and flag any data quality concerns.
Provide code (Python/Pandas or SQL) for each answer so I can reproduce results.

docs.title: Segmentation Analysis
docs.text:
Segment my [CUSTOMERS/USERS/TRANSACTIONS] data by [DIMENSION].

Data context:
- [ENTITY] table with [KEY COLUMNS]
- Time period: [START] to [END]
- Metrics of interest: [LIST - e.g., revenue, frequency, retention]

For each segment, compute:
- Segment size and percentage of total
- Average [METRIC 1], [METRIC 2], [METRIC 3]
- Month-over-month growth rate
- Top 3 distinguishing characteristics

Identify the highest-value segment and the fastest-growing segment. Provide the SQL or Python needed to reproduce.

docs.title: Query from Plain English
docs.text:
Convert the following business question into a SQL query for [DATABASE TYPE - PostgreSQL/BigQuery/Snowflake/MySQL].

Question: [PLAIN ENGLISH QUESTION]

Available tables:
[TABLE NAME 1]: [COLUMNS WITH TYPES]
[TABLE NAME 2]: [COLUMNS WITH TYPES]
[JOIN RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN TABLES]

Requirements:
- Use explicit JOIN syntax, not implicit joins
- Include comments explaining each CTE or subquery
- Handle NULL values appropriately
- Add query optimization notes if the query would scan large tables
- Format output as [DESIRED FORMAT - daily time series, top-N ranking, summary statistics]

Expected output columns: [DESCRIBE EACH]

docs.title: Query Optimization
docs.text:
Analyze and optimize this slow query:

[PASTE SLOW QUERY]

Execution context:
- Database: [TYPE AND VERSION]
- Table sizes: [TABLE 1: X rows, TABLE 2: Y rows]
- Current execution time: [DURATION]
- Target: [DURATION]
- Available indexes: [LIST EXISTING INDEXES]

Identify the bottleneck (full table scan, nested loop join, sort, etc.).
Provide the optimized query and explain what changed and why it's faster.
Suggest any new indexes (with CREATE INDEX statements) that would help.

docs.title: Automated Report Template
docs.text:
Design a [WEEKLY/MONTHLY/QUARTERLY] report for [STAKEHOLDER ROLE].

Metrics to include:
1. [METRIC 1] - [DEFINITION, TARGET, PREVIOUS PERIOD VALUE]
2. [METRIC 2] - [DEFINITION, TARGET, PREVIOUS PERIOD VALUE]
3. [ETC.]

For each metric provide:
- Current value and period-over-period change (%)
- The SQL query or data source it comes from
- A plain-language interpretation (what changed and why it matters)
- A red/yellow/green status indicator with threshold definitions

Include an executive summary section (max 200 words) synthesizing the key takeaways.

docs.title: Chart and Visualization Guidance
docs.text:
I need to visualize [DATA RELATIONSHIP - e.g., "revenue by channel over 12 months"].

Data characteristics:
- [N] categories
- [TIME GRANULARITY] time dimension
- [CONTINUOUS/DISCRETE] values
- Comparison: [ABSOLUTE VALUES / PERCENT CHANGE / VS TARGET]

Recommend:
1. The best chart type with justification (bar, line, area, scatter, heatmap, etc.)
2. Color scheme considerations (accessibility, brand alignment)
3. Labeling strategy (axis titles, data labels, annotations)
4. What the viewer should notice first - design for the "3-second test"

Provide the code to generate this in [PLOTLY/MATPLOTLIB/VEGA-LITE/EXCEL].

docs.title: KPI Definition and Calculation
docs.text:
Define and calculate [METRIC NAME] for [BUSINESS CONTEXT].

Provide:
1. Plain-English definition that a non-technical stakeholder would understand
2. Mathematical formula with clear numerator and denominator
3. SQL query (or Python) that computes it from [TABLE NAMES]
4. Common pitfalls in calculation (e.g., double-counting, time window edge cases)
5. How often it should be recalculated and what refresh latency is acceptable
6. Related metrics to track alongside it for context

Benchmark: what's a "good" value for a company of our [SIZE/STAGE/INDUSTRY]?

docs.title: Anomaly Detection
docs.text:
Analyze this time series data for anomalies:

[PASTE DATA OR DESCRIBE SOURCE]
Metric: [METRIC NAME]
Granularity: [HOURLY/DAILY/WEEKLY]
Expected pattern: [SEASONALITY, TREND, KNOWN EVENTS]

Use [METHOD - z-score/IQR/moving average/STL decomposition] to detect anomalies.
For each anomaly found:
- Date/time and observed vs expected value
- Magnitude (how many standard deviations from baseline)
- Possible explanation based on known events in that period
- Recommended action (investigate further, ignore as noise, escalate)

Provide code to run this detection on an ongoing schedule.

docs.title: Executive summary prompts
docs.text:
These are the high-leverage, broad-scope prompts. They fire CorpusIQ's multi-source skills - pre-built runbooks that pull from everything you have connected and synthesize a single answer.

If you only learn one category, learn this one.

docs.text: What this does: Runs a top-to-bottom snapshot - cash, revenue trend, wins, risks, this-week priorities. Sample answer shape: Section headers for cash position, revenue, top wins, top risks, focus-this-week - each with 2-4 bullets and specific numbers from your data.

docs.text: What this does: Same engine as above, formatted for skimming. Good for forwarding to a co-founder. Connectors used: Whatever you have connected. Behind the scenes: executive-snapshot. Sample answer shape: Tighter than the health check - one screen, no fluff.

docs.title: "What changed in the business this month?"
docs.text: What this does: Diff-style report - what moved up, what moved down, what's new on the radar. Connectors used: QuickBooks, Shopify, GA4, ad accounts, CRM. Behind the scenes: executive-snapshot with a month-over-month framing. Sample answer shape: Two columns - improvements and regressions - with the metric, the delta, and a one-line possible cause.

docs.text: What this does: Ranks the top 3 things to do based on revenue impact, deadlines, and what's slipping. Cross-references calendar, pipeline, overdue tasks, and high-value unanswered emails. Connectors used: Calendar, CRM, Email, QuickBooks. Behind the scenes: today-focus skill. Sample answer shape: A ranked list of 3 items with reasoning per item ("Follow up with Acme - $42K deal, last touch 11 days ago").

Connectors used: Shopify, Email (Gmail/Outlook), Calendar, QuickBooks. Behind the scenes: morning-briefing skill. docs.title: MCP developer prompts
docs.text:
These prompts are written for developers using CorpusIQ as an MCP server - either from Claude Desktop, a custom MCP client, or an agent pipeline. They go beyond operator-level queries and focus on programmatic access, cross-connector joins, debugging, and building CorpusIQ into larger workflows.

If you're new to MCP, see MCP architecture.

docs.title: "List all tools available for the Shopify connector."
docs.text: MCP call: resolve_connector with intent "list Shopify tools" What this does: Returns the exact tool schemas callable against Shopify. Useful as a discovery step before building a pipeline that needs specific Shopify fields. Developer use case: Enumerate available actions before generating tool-call code in your agent.

docs.title: "Fetch all orders from the last 30 days and return them as structured JSON."
docs.text: Connectors used: Shopify or Amazon Seller. MCP tool: get_orders with created_after date param. What this does: Returns raw order objects with line items, amounts, statuses. The MCP layer returns typed JSON - no parsing of prose needed. Developer use case: Feed order data into a downstream analytics pipeline or a fine-tuning dataset.

docs.title: "Pull GA4 sessions by channel for the last 90 days, grouped by date."
docs.text: Connectors used: GA4. MCP tool: run_report with dimensions ["date", "sessionDefaultChannelGroup"] and metric ["sessions"]. What this does: Returns a per-day, per-channel session matrix. Developer use case: Build a channel attribution table without a separate BI tool.

docs.title: "Return QuickBooks P&L for Q1 as structured data."
docs.text: Connectors used: QuickBooks. MCP tool: get_profit_loss with start_date and end_date. What this does: Returns income, cost of goods, expenses, and net profit as a structured report object. Developer use case: Ingest into a spreadsheet, dashboard, or financial model automatically.

docs.title: "Get all active HubSpot deals with their amounts and pipeline stage."
docs.text: Connectors used: HubSpot. MCP tool: list_hubspot_deals with pagination. What this does: Returns deal ID, name, amount, stage, and owner for every open deal. Developer use case: Build a pipeline forecast tool that refreshes from live CRM data.

docs.title: "List every Klaviyo campaign sent in the last 60 days with open and click rates."
docs.text: Connectors used: Klaviyo. MCP tool: get_campaigns with start_date and end_date. What this does: Returns campaign objects with recipient count, open rate, click rate, and revenue attribution. Developer use case: Automate an email performance report that runs on a schedule.

docs.title: "Join Shopify order revenue to Meta Ads spend by date and compute ROAS."
docs.text: Connectors used: Shopify, Meta Ads. MCP tools: get_orders (Shopify) + get_account_insights (Meta Ads) with matching date ranges. What this does: Two separate MCP calls return parallel date-keyed datasets. Your agent joins on date and computes ROAS = revenue / spend. Developer use case: Build a custom attribution model that doesn't rely on Meta's self-reported ROAS.

docs.title: "Compare GA4 sessions on email send days to non-send days."
docs.text: Connectors used: Klaviyo, GA4. MCP tool (built-in cross-source): correlate_email_vs_web_traffic. What this does: Returns a day-level table: email sent (bool), GA4 sessions, delta from baseline. Developer use case: Validate email's halo effect on organic traffic before attributing it as a channel.

docs.title: "Join QuickBooks invoices to HubSpot deals to find deals that closed but were never invoiced."
docs.text: Connectors used: HubSpot, QuickBooks. MCP tools: list_hubspot_deals (filter: stage=closed-won) + list_invoices (QuickBooks). What this does: Two lists, joined on company name or amount. Gaps are deals with no matching invoice. Developer use case: Revenue leakage audit - catch won deals that slipped through billing.

docs.title: "Pull every Stripe charge and match to QuickBooks income lines."
docs.text: Connectors used: Stripe, QuickBooks. MCP tools: list_charges (Stripe) + get_profit_loss or list_invoices (QuickBooks). What this does: Stripe returns raw charges; QuickBooks returns booked income. Mismatches surface timing gaps or missing entries. Developer use case: Automated reconciliation check - run daily in a CI pipeline.

docs.title: "Show me Klaviyo list growth alongside Facebook ad spend to see if paid ads are growing my list."
docs.text: Connectors used: Klaviyo, Meta Ads. MCP tool (built-in cross-source): correlate_form_signups_vs_ad_traffic. What this does: Returns form submit counts and Meta spend per day. Developer use case: Validate paid-to-list growth attribution.

docs.title: "Why is my Shopify connector returning zero orders?"
docs.text: Connectors used: Shopify. Debug approach: Call get_orders with an explicit wide date range (created_after = 90 days ago). If still zero, call get_connector_status and check for token expiry or scope issues. Common causes: Token revoked in Shopify admin, wrong store domain configured, date filter is too narrow by default.

docs.title: "My GA4 report is returning empty rows - how do I debug it?"
docs.text: Connectors used: GA4. Debug approach: First call list_accounts to verify the property is visible. Then call list_properties with the account ID. Then run a minimal report: single dimension date, single metric sessions, last 7 days. If that works, add dimensions one at a time until the empty response reappears. Common cause: property_id has the format properties/XXXXXXX - make sure you're passing just the numeric ID, not the full path.

docs.title: "Check whether my QuickBooks token is still valid."
docs.text: MCP tool: get_company_info - this is the lightest QuickBooks call. A valid token returns company name and fiscal year. An expired token returns a 401 error, which tells you to re-authenticate via get_connector_status.

docs.title: "List all connectors and their current auth status."
docs.text: MCP tool: get_connector_status (no parameters). What this does: Returns a table of every configured connector, its auth state (connected / expired / not authenticated), and a re-auth link where applicable. Developer use case: Health check endpoint in an agent - run this at session start to gate which connectors are usable.

docs.title: "Why are my Meta Ads impressions different between the account summary and the campaign-level report?"
docs.text: Connectors used: Meta Ads. Debug approach: get_account_insights aggregates across all campaigns including deleted/archived. list_campaigns with status_filter=ALL then get_campaign_insights per campaign will surface whether deleted campaigns are inflating the account total. Fix: Filter campaigns by status_filter=ACTIVE for apples-to-apples.

docs.title: Building agent workflows with CorpusIQ as the knowledge layer
"Build an agent that answers CFO questions using live QuickBooks + Stripe data."
docs.text: Architecture: 1. Connect Claude (or your LLM) to CorpusIQ MCP at https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp. 2. Authenticate QuickBooks and Stripe connectors. 3. The agent calls get_profit_loss, get_balance_sheet, list_charges, and get_balance as needed, grounded in live data. No ETL required. CorpusIQ handles the OAuth tokens, rate limiting, and data normalization.

docs.title: "Build a daily business digest that fires at 8am and pulls from 5 connectors."
docs.text: Architecture: 1. Cron job (or scheduler) sends a prompt to your MCP-connected LLM at 8am. 2. Prompt: "Run the executive snapshot skill." 3. CorpusIQ's executive-snapshot skill pulls QuickBooks, Shopify, HubSpot, ad accounts, and GA4 automatically. 4. The LLM returns a formatted digest. Push to Slack, email, or Notion. MCP skill trigger: invoke_skill with skill_name="executive-snapshot".

docs.title: "Build a Slack bot that answers revenue questions."
docs.text: Architecture: 1. Slack bot receives a message like "how did we do last week?" 2. Bot forwards the message to an LLM with CorpusIQ MCP attached. 3. CorpusIQ calls Shopify + QuickBooks, returns structured revenue data. 4. LLM composes a Slack-formatted reply. Bot posts it. Key connector: get_profit_loss + get_orders for revenue. Read-only guarantee: CorpusIQ cannot post to Slack, only read.

docs.title: "Use CorpusIQ as the memory layer for a sales agent - give it access to all open deals and customer history."
docs.text: Architecture: 1. Attach CorpusIQ MCP to your sales agent's LLM context. 2. On each call, the agent resolves which connectors to query via resolve_connector. 3. list_hubspot_deals, get_hubspot_contact, list_invoices (QuickBooks), and list_gmail_messages give the agent a 360-degree view of each account. Why MCP beats RAG here: Data is live, not stale embeddings. The agent always sees the current deal stage, latest invoice status, and most recent email thread.

docs.title: "Expose CorpusIQ data to a custom dashboard without a backend."
docs.text: Architecture: 1. Use any MCP client library (e.g. @modelcontextprotocol/client-typescript). 2. Connect to https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp with your CorpusIQ JWT. 3. Call tools directly from your frontend or edge function. 4. Render the returned JSON in your dashboard components. No separate API to build. CorpusIQ's MCP layer is the API.

docs.title: "Run a competitive SEO audit on demand from a CI pipeline."
docs.text:
Connectors used: Semrush, Search Console, GA4. MCP tools: get_domain_overview, get_competitors, get_performance. Architecture: 1. CI job calls your MCP-connected LLM with: "Run an SEO health check and flag any position drops > 5 places since last week." 2. CorpusIQ pulls live Semrush + GSC data, compares to prior run (stored in canonical facts), and returns a diff report. 3. CI job posts the report to Slack or opens a GitHub issue on regressions.

docs.title: Research Prompts - Competitive Analysis & Market Intelligence
Competitor Deep-Dive
docs.text:
Conduct a structured competitive analysis of [COMPETITOR NAME] in [INDUSTRY/MARKET].

Research dimensions:
1. Company overview: founding year, headquarters, funding, employee count, leadership
2. Product: feature set, differentiators, pricing model, user experience strengths and weaknesses
3. Market position: target customer, market share estimate, growth trajectory
4. Go-to-market: primary channels, content strategy, sales motion (self-serve vs sales-led)
5. Strengths: what they do better than alternatives
6. Weaknesses: gaps, customer complaints, churn signals
7. Recent moves: last 6 months of product launches, partnerships, pricing changes

Sources to consider: website, G2/Capterra reviews, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, press releases, job postings.

Format as an actionable brief. For each weakness identified, note whether it's an opportunity for us to exploit.

docs.title: Competitive Landscape Map
docs.text:
Map the competitive landscape for [MARKET/PRODUCT CATEGORY].

Analyze [N] competitors: [LIST NAMES IF KNOWN]

Create a positioning matrix with these axes:
- X-axis: [DIMENSION 1 - e.g., Ease of Use / Power]
- Y-axis: [DIMENSION 2 - e.g., SMB Focus / Enterprise Focus]

For each competitor:
- Bubble size proportional to [REVENUE/USER BASE/MARKET SHARE]
- Primary customer segment
- Price point: [FREE/FREEMIUM/$XX-YY/MONTH/ENTERPRISE]
- Key differentiator (one sentence)
- Where they're vulnerable

Identify whitespace on the matrix - where are the underserved customer needs?

docs.title: Feature Comparison Matrix
docs.text:
Create a feature comparison matrix for [PRODUCT CATEGORY].

Competitors: [LIST 3-6 COMPETITORS]
Feature categories:
1. [CORE FEATURE AREA 1]
2. [CORE FEATURE AREA 2]
3. [INTEGRATIONS/ECOSYSTEM]
4. [SECURITY/COMPLIANCE]
5. [PRICING/MONETIZATION]

Use a table format: Features as rows, competitors as columns. Mark each cell: ✓ (full support), ◐ (partial/limited), ✗ (not available), ? (unclear).

Below the table: highlight the 3 biggest feature gaps in the market and our relative position on each.

docs.title: TAM/SAM/SOM Analysis
docs.text:
Estimate the TAM, SAM, and SOM for [PRODUCT/SERVICE] in [GEOGRAPHY/INDUSTRY].

Product description: [1-2 SENTENCES]
Target customer: [WHO BUYS THIS]

Provide:
1. TAM (Total Addressable Market): Top-down estimate using industry reports and government data
   - Methodology and assumptions
   - Source citations
   - Dollar figure with confidence range

2. SAM (Serviceable Addressable Market): TAM filtered by our target segment and geography
   - Filters applied (company size, industry, budget, etc.)
   - Resulting figure

3. SOM (Serviceable Obtainable Market): Realistic share we can capture in [YEAR]
   - Assumptions about penetration rate and competition
   - Resulting revenue estimate

Note: if specific data isn't available, state your assumptions clearly and provide a sensitivity range.

docs.title: Market Trends Report
docs.text:
Synthesize a market trends report on [TOPIC/INDUSTRY] for the next [TIME HORIZON].

Structure:
1. Executive summary: 3 most important shifts happening right now
2. Trend 1: [NAME] - driving factors, evidence, implications
3. Trend 2: [NAME] - driving factors, evidence, implications
4. Trend 3: [NAME] - driving factors, evidence, implications
5. Wildcards: low-probability high-impact events to watch
6. Implications: what this means for [OUR BUSINESS/INVESTMENT THESIS]

Each trend should include:
- Supporting data points from recent reports or news
- Companies or products exemplifying the trend
- Contrarian view (what would prove this trend wrong)
- Recommended action

Cite specific sources with dates. Flag any contradictory signals.

docs.title: Tool/Framework Selection
docs.text:
Evaluate [CANDIDATE TOOLS/FRAMEWORKS] for [USE CASE].

Context:
- Team size and skills: [DESCRIBE]
- Scale requirements: [USERS/REQUESTS/DATA VOLUME]
- Budget constraints: [RANGE]
- Timeline: [WHEN DECISION NEEDED]

Evaluation criteria with weights (must sum to 100%):
1. Functional fit: [%] - does it solve the core problem?
2. Learning curve: [%] - time to team proficiency
3. Community/ecosystem: [%] - available libraries, support, hiring pool
4. Performance: [%] - latency, throughput, resource usage
5. Cost: [%] - licensing, hosting, operational
6. Future-proofing: [%] - roadmap, vendor stability, migration ease

Score each candidate 1-5 per criterion. Provide weighted total and a narrative recommendation.
Include a "what would make us switch later" section.

docs.title: Build vs Buy Analysis
docs.text:
Analyze whether we should build or buy a solution for [PROBLEM DESCRIPTION].

Internal build estimate:
- Engineering effort: [PERSON-MONTHS]
- Ongoing maintenance: [HOURS/MONTH]
- Opportunity cost: [WHAT ELSE THE TEAM COULD BUILD]

Buy options:
- Vendor 1: [NAME] at [$XX/MONTH] - pros/cons
- Vendor 2: [NAME] at [$XX/MONTH] - pros/cons

Decision framework:
1. Core vs context: is this differentiating for our business?
2. Time to value: when does each option deliver?
3. Total cost over [3-YEAR] horizon (build: eng cost + infra; buy: license + integration)
4. Flexibility risk: what if requirements change?
5. Vendor risk: what if they raise prices, get acquired, or shut down?

Provide a clear recommendation with the decisive factor highlighted.

docs.title: Literature Review Summary
docs.text:
Synthesize findings from these [N] sources on [TOPIC]:

[LIST OR DESCRIBE SOURCES]

Output:
1. Consensus findings (things most sources agree on)
2. Points of disagreement or debate
3. Gaps - questions none of the sources adequately address
4. Key quotes (max 5, with attribution)
5. Recommended follow-up research questions

Keep total output to [N] words. Prioritize actionable insights over comprehensive summary.

docs.title: SWOT Analysis
docs.text:
Generate a SWOT analysis for [COMPANY/PRODUCT/INITIATIVE].

Context: [1-2 PARAGRAPHS OF BACKGROUND]

Format:
- Strengths (internal, positive): [4-6 items] - what advantages do we have?
- Weaknesses (internal, negative): [4-6 items] - where are we vulnerable?
- Opportunities (external, positive): [4-6 items] - what trends or gaps can we exploit?
- Threats (external, negative): [4-6 items] - what external forces could harm us?

For each quadrant, prioritize by impact and likelihood. 
Then provide a TOWS cross-analysis:
- How do we use strengths to exploit opportunities?
- How do we use strengths to counter threats?
- How do we fix weaknesses to pursue opportunities?
- How do we fix weaknesses to survive threats?

docs.title: process_submissions.py - Community Submission Pipeline
docs.text:
Validates and ingests community-submitted repositories, skills, and MCP servers. Checks for duplicates, validates metadata, and generates pull requests for approved submissions.

Usage:

python3 process_submissions.py --test   # Score a sample submission end to end
python3 process_submissions.py --issue 12   # Process one specific submission issue

docs.title: promote_submission.py - Human-Judgement Promotion
docs.text:
The submission scorer reads only a repository's name, description, and topics, so a repo that genuinely works with Hermes but never names it in metadata scores low and is rejected. This is the manual path that closes that gap: it takes a repo already in the review queue, records why it was promoted, and rewrites every downstream file in one transaction.

Usage:

python3 promote_submission.py --repo owner/name --note "why this was promoted by hand"
python3 promote_submission.py --repo owner/name --note "reason" --category tools --dry-run

docs.title: integrate_approved.py - Publish Auto-Approved Repos
docs.text:
discover.py auto-approves repos into data/approved_repos.json but never writes the directory page. This script finds approved repos that are missing from the directory and writes them into ecosystem/index.md, star-sorted, using the same block builder as promote_submission.py.

Usage:

python3 integrate_approved.py                  # Write all missing approved repos
python3 integrate_approved.py --dry-run        # Show what would be written
python3 integrate_approved.py --limit 20       # Cap the number of entries written

docs.title: finish_promotion.py - Complete a Partial Promotion
docs.text:
promote_submission.py writes the JSON stores first and the files last. If the file phase fails, this completes it from the approved row. Safe to rerun: both writers skip work that is already done.

Usage:

python3 finish_promotion.py            # Finish the default pending promotion
python3 finish_promotion.py owner/name # Finish a specific repo

docs.title: Security and Read-Only Access
docs.text:
CorpusIQ is built on one rule: it reads, and it never acts.

Every connector uses read-only OAuth. CorpusIQ can retrieve data from your connected business tools, but it cannot write to them, modify them, or execute anything inside them.

One boundary worth stating precisely: external retrieval is read-only, and configuration controls can write scoped platform state. Enabling or disabling a connector, or re-authorizing one, changes a setting inside your CorpusIQ account. It never changes a record in Shopify, Stripe, QuickBooks, or any other connected system.

docs.title: Security, Read-Only Access, and What CorpusIQ Never Does
docs.text:
CorpusIQ is built on one rule: it reads, and it never acts.

This page is the complete answer to the questions customers ask most: can CorpusIQ change anything in my systems? Does it retain my data? Can it act like an AI agent? The answer to all three is no.

docs.title: CorpusIQ uses read-only access on every connection
docs.text:
Every connector uses read-only OAuth. CorpusIQ can retrieve data from your connected business tools. It cannot write to them, modify them, or execute anything inside them.

  • No campaign changes. CorpusIQ cannot create, edit, or pause ads in Google Ads, Meta, or any advertising platform.
  • No budget changes. Bidding, budgets, and targeting are never touched.
  • No data writes. CorpusIQ never creates records, updates fields, or deletes anything in QuickBooks, Shopify, Stripe, or any other system.
  • No file edits. Documents, sheets, and emails are read only.

docs.title: CorpusIQ is not an AI agent
docs.text:
An AI agent takes actions on your behalf. CorpusIQ does not.

CorpusIQ only allows ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, or another AI client to securely read the business data you authorized. The AI client is the conversation layer. CorpusIQ is the governed intelligence layer that decides which systems get checked, validates the data, and returns a verified answer. There is no execution capability inside CorpusIQ.

If you ever want an AI system to take actions, write data, or execute workflows, you would use a separate external AI agent. That agent could use CorpusIQ through a direct MCP connection to securely read the business data it needs, and then act through its own integrations.

docs.title: Retention: raw data is not retained
docs.text:
Data passes through CorpusIQ on demand.

When you ask a question, the authorized data is retrieved from your systems, processed for the answer, and returned to your AI client as read-only information. CorpusIQ uses read-only access for direct MCP live retrieval. It does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; operational logs retain query text, per-user tool-call metadata, and bounded outcome summaries for up to 30 days. There is no warehouse, no data lake, and no retention of your business records beyond those scoped operational logs.

docs.title: No one at CorpusIQ can access your accounts
docs.text: Your connections are yours. The OAuth authorization you approve is scoped to your account, and no CorpusIQ staff member can access or read your connected systems. The data flows from your systems to your AI client through CorpusIQ, on demand, without human access.

docs.title: Why this is intentional
docs.text:
CorpusIQ's business model is designed to avoid the security and liability risks of allowing AI to write to or execute actions inside customer systems. Read-only access means:

  • No risk of accidental writes or destructive actions
  • No data retention liability
  • No privilege escalation surface
  • Answers you can trust, because the data was never modified

docs.title: How the read-only guarantee is enforced
docs.text:
1. Read-only OAuth scopes on every connector. CorpusIQ requests only the permissions needed to read data, never to modify it.
  2. No mutation endpoints. The CorpusIQ server exposes no path that can write to a connected system.
  3. On-demand passthrough. Data is fetched per question and returned, not collected or stored.
  4. Independent authentication. Each connector authenticates separately under your account, with no shared credentials.

One boundary worth stating precisely: external retrieval is read-only, and configuration controls can write scoped platform state. Enabling or disabling a connector, or re-authorizing one, changes a setting inside your CorpusIQ account. It never changes a record in Shopify, Stripe, QuickBooks, or any other connected system.

docs.title: AI Business Intelligence: Connect Your Tools to ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity
docs.text:
Your business runs on data. Shopify orders. Stripe payments. QuickBooks financials. HubSpot deals. GA4 analytics. Meta Ads performance. All of it lives in different tools with different logins and different dashboards.

AI business intelligence changes this. Connect your tools once. Ask any AI your business questions. Get one consistent answer with every source cited.

docs.title: How AI Business Intelligence Works
docs.text:
Traditional business intelligence requires dashboards. You pull data from each tool into a central platform. You build reports. You train your team. You spend hours reconciling numbers that should already agree.

AI business intelligence eliminates the dashboard entirely. You ask questions in plain English. The AI queries your actual business tools in real time. Returns one answer. Cites every source. Same answer regardless of which AI you use.

Revenue questions: "What was revenue last month?" The AI queries Shopify, Stripe, and QuickBooks simultaneously. Returns one number with the breakdown. Shopify: $89K. Stripe: $38K. QuickBooks: $15K. Total: $142K.

Customer questions: "Which customers are at risk of churning?" The AI queries your CRM for engagement data, your billing system for payment history, and your support tool for ticket volume. Returns a ranked list with the evidence.

Marketing questions: "What is our actual ROAS across all channels?" The AI queries Meta Ads, Google Ads, Shopify, and GA4. Attributes revenue to spend. Returns blended and per-channel numbers.

docs.title: Why AI BI Beats Traditional BI
docs.text:
No dashboards to build. You do not need a BI team. You do not need to learn Tableau or Looker. You ask questions. You get answers.

No raw-data warehouse. Direct MCP does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads. Every query fetches live data, while scoped operational logs may be retained for up to 30 days. Optional indexed search has a separate embeddings and minimal-metadata lifecycle.

No reconciliation sessions. When every AI pulls from the same sources using the same definitions, the numbers match. Revenue means the same thing in ChatGPT as it does in Claude as it does in Perplexity.

docs.title: Google Preferred Sources Badge
docs.text:
Google lets readers mark a site as a preferred source. Once a reader picks your site, your content can show a "preferred" badge in AI Overviews, AI Mode, Top Stories, and Google Discover.

This page explains what the feature is, why it matters for AI-era search, and how to add it to any site in two lines of code.

docs.title: What is a preferred source?
docs.text:
Preferred sources is a Google Search feature. Users select the sites they trust in Google's source preferences tool. After that, content from those sites is more likely to appear in:

  • AI Overviews and AI Mode, highlighted with a preferred badge
  • Top Stories, with a preferred badge
  • Google Discover

It is a reader-driven signal. The reader chooses, and Google surfaces more of your content for that reader.

docs.title: Why it matters for AEO and GEO
docs.text:
Answer engines and generative engines cite sources they can trust. A preferred badge does two things:

  1. It puts your site in front of readers who already trust you, in the exact surfaces where AI answers appear.
  2. It signals to Google that real users actively select your content.

For business tools sites, this targets the same surfaces as AEO and GEO work: AI Overviews, AI Mode, and conversational search.

docs.title: Eligibility
docs.text:
Only domain-level and subdomain-level sites are eligible. Subdirectory paths are not.

Google also requires the site to be included in Search generative AI features in Search Console before it can appear in the source preferences tool.

  • Eligible: https://example.com, https://code.example.com
  • Not eligible: https://example.com/blog

docs.title: Implementation (standard, recommended)
docs.text:
Two lines. Add the library script to the head:

<script async src="https://news.google.com/swg/js/v1/publisher.js"></script>

Add the button where you want it in the body:

<div google-add-preferred-source-btn></div>

That is it. The button is auto-localized and Google-styled.

docs.title: Dark theme
docs.text: <div google-add-preferred-source-btn data-theme="dark"></div>

docs.title: Language override
docs.text: <div google-add-preferred-source-btn data-lang="en"></div>

docs.title: Deeplink (no code)
docs.text:
For social posts, newsletters, and emails, use the deeplink format:

https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://yourdomain.com

Readers click, add your site, and get returned to your page.

docs.title: Advanced usage
docs.text:
For custom UI, the library also ships as an ES module with a programmatic API:

import { preferredSource } from "https://news.google.com/swg/js/v1/publisher.mjs";

preferredSource.init({ theme: "dark", lang: "en" });

Or bind to any click handler:

button.onclick = () => { preferredSource.addPreferredSource(); };

docs.text:
• Google Search Central guide: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/preferred-sources
  • Source preferences tool: https://www.google.com/preferences/source

docs.title: Hermes Agent Setup & Installation Guide - Get Started Fast
docs.text: Hermes Agent runs on everything from a $50 Raspberry Pi to a $20,000 DGX workstation. This setup guide helps you pick the right hardware platform, install Hermes Agent in under 5 minutes, and choose the best model configuration for your needs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Don't overthink it. If you're just getting started, use whatever machine you already have - a MacBook, a Windows desktop, or even a $5/month VPS. Hermes Agent is designed to be provider-agnostic and hardware-flexible. You can always migrate later to a different setup platform.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Hermes Agent installs from a signed desktop package or a one-line install script, then connects to AI models through one of three paths:

Path How It Works Cost Ollama (local) Run open-source models directly on your hardware via Ollama Free OpenRouter Access 200+ models through a single API gateway - pay-per-token $0-$20+/month Direct provider Connect directly to Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, or other model providers Varies by provider

After installation, Hermes Agent uses skills (reusable workflows), crons (scheduled automation), MCP servers (external tool connections), and memory systems to operate autonomously.

docs.title: Choosing Your Setup
docs.text:
Three questions to decide:

  1. Do you have a GPU? If yes, run models locally for free with Ollama. If no, use API-based cloud models via OpenRouter.
  2. Does it need to run 24/7? If yes, pick a cloud VPS, Raspberry Pi, or always-on desktop. If no, your laptop or gaming PC works fine.
  3. What's your budget? $0/month (existing hardware + Ollama), ~$5/month (cloud VPS + free-tier models), or $20+/month (cloud VPS + Claude-level models).

docs.title: Quick Start (Any Machine)
docs.text:
This gets Hermes Agent running on any Linux, macOS, or Windows machine. The installer provisions its own pinned Python and toolchain, so a system-wide Python install is not required.

# 1. Install (Linux, macOS, WSL2)
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
# Windows PowerShell: iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1)

# 2. Create a profile
hermes profile create my-agent
hermes profile use my-agent

# 3. Configure a model provider (pick one)
# Option A: Nous Portal - one login covers a model plus the Tool Gateway
hermes setup --portal

# Option B: OpenRouter - instant access to 200+ models
hermes config set OPENROUTER_API_KEY "your-key"

# Option C: Direct provider - Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, and others
hermes config set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY "your-key"

# Option D: Ollama - free, local, no API key needed
ollama pull llama3.2

# 4. Choose your default model
hermes model

# 5. Verify
hermes --version
hermes doctor

That's it. You can now use Hermes Agent interactively. For persistent operation (crons, gateway, messaging), continue to the setup guide for your platform.

• Provider-agnostic: Switch between Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama, and 200+ models without changing your code
  • Hardware-flexible: Run on anything from a Raspberry Pi to a DGX workstation
  • Zero-friction migration: Start on your laptop, move to a cloud VPS later
  • Free tier available: Use Ollama for local, free model inference
  • Autonomous operation: Cron scheduling + MCP tools + skills for 24/7 automation

docs.title: Detailed Setup Guides
docs.text:
Choose your hardware:

  • Mac Mini M4 (Standalone) - All-in-one: models, browser automation, crons. Best for solo founders.
  • Gaming PC / Desktop - Max GPU performance with CUDA. Best for developers with powerful rigs.
  • Cloud VPS - $5-20/month, always-on. Best for budget production use.
  • Raspberry Pi 5 - Ultra-low-cost 24/7 agent. Best for lightweight automation.
  • Docker - Containerized deployment. Best for reproducibility and CI/CD.
  • Windows 11 + WSL2 - Windows users, Linux-native experience. Best for Windows desktops.

docs.title: After Setup
docs.text:
Once Hermes Agent is running, add capabilities:

  • Session Cleanup - Delete or prune old sessions and reclaim state.db disk space
  • Backup and Restore - Native hermes backup snapshots, full archives, and hermes import restore
  • MCP Integration - Connect to Gmail, Slack, databases, and 40+ platforms
  • CorpusIQ MCP Setup - Connect 40+ business tools to Hermes in 5 minutes
  • CorpusIQ Cron Patterns - Autonomous business monitoring with Hermes + CorpusIQ
  • CorpusIQ Troubleshooting - Token refresh, 401 errors, fork restrictions
  • Cron Scheduling - Schedule autonomous tasks with cron design best practices
  • Skills Marketplace - Add community-built capabilities and create custom skills

docs.title: What is Hermes Agent?
docs.text: Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent framework by Nous Research that connects to language models (local or cloud) and external tools through MCP (Model Context Protocol). It automates tasks through skills, scheduled crons, and multi-source data queries.

docs.title: Can I run Hermes Agent for free?
docs.text: Yes. Install Hermes Agent on your existing hardware, pull free models from Ollama (like Llama 3.2), and you pay nothing. Cloud API usage is optional and pay-per-use.

docs.title: Which hardware is best for Hermes Agent?
docs.text: The Mac Mini M4 is the recommended all-in-one platform. For budget 24/7 operation, a cloud VPS at $5-20/month works well. For maximum GPU performance, use a gaming PC with CUDA.

docs.title: How do I connect Hermes Agent to business data?
docs.text: Use the MCP Integration Guide to connect 40+ business platforms - CRM, email, analytics, databases, advertising, and more - through a single OAuth flow with CorpusIQ MCP.

docs.title: What's the difference between Ollama and OpenRouter?
docs.text: Ollama runs models locally on your hardware (free, private, limited to smaller models). OpenRouter provides API access to 200+ models including frontier models like Claude and GPT-4o (pay-per-use, no hardware requirements).

docs.title: How do I keep Hermes Agent running 24/7?
docs.text: Use a cloud VPS, Raspberry Pi, or an always-on desktop with caffeinate (macOS) or power settings adjusted. Configure the Hermes gateway as a systemd or launchd service for automatic restart.

docs.title: How do I add new capabilities after setup?
docs.text: Extend Hermes Agent through MCP servers for external tools, skills for reusable workflows, crons for scheduled automation, and memory systems for persistent context.

docs.title: Hermes Backup and Restore - Native Commands and Snapshots
docs.text:
Hermes Agent ships two backup paths and two matching restore paths, with no extra tooling required. Use them before an upgrade, before editing configuration that could break a running agent, and on a schedule if the machine holds work you cannot rebuild.

This page documents the built-in commands, what each one actually captures, what it deliberately leaves out, and how to restore. If you would rather use a community script with its own retention logic, see the full backup script guide or the backup and recovery skill instead.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
What you want Command Output Restore with Fast snapshot of critical state hermes backup --quick A state snapshot directory /snapshot restore <id> in a CLI session Complete portable archive hermes backup A .zip file hermes import <zipfile>

Both commands operate on the active Hermes home directory, which defaults to ~/.hermes and is overridden by HERMES_HOME. Both take a cross-process lock, so you cannot corrupt a backup by running one while the gateway is up.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Component Quick snapshot Full backup Storage state-snapshots/<timestamp>-<label>/ inside the Hermes home One .zip at the path you choose Typical size Megabytes - state and config only Depends on sessions and media; can be gigabytes Skills and sessions Not included Included SQLite databases Included (key state files only) Included (every database) Portable to another machine Not by itself - it is a local recovery point Yes - that is the point of the zip Retention 20 most recent snapshots --keep N, default 3 archives

Two details matter more than the table:

  1. Live SQLite databases are copied with sqlite3.backup(), not by reading the file. That produces a consistent database image while the gateway is writing to it. The -wal, -shm and -journal sidecars are therefore excluded on purpose: pairing a fresh snapshot with a stale sidecar is what produces a torn restore on the next open.
  2. The codebase is never archived. hermes-agent, nested .git directories, node_modules, virtualenvs, Python bytecode and tool caches are all skipped, because they are reinstallable. A backup is your data, not your program.

docs.title: Quick State Snapshot
docs.text:
hermes backup --quick does not write a zip. It writes a state snapshot, which is the same mechanism the updater uses as its pre-update safety net.

# Snapshot with a label you will recognise later
hermes backup --quick --label before-upgrade

Real output from a run:

State snapshot created: 20261106-194536-before-upgrade
  2 snapshot(s) stored in ~/.hermes/profiles/<profile>/state-snapshots/
  Restore with: /snapshot restore 20261106-194536-before-upgrade

Restoring a snapshot happens inside a Hermes CLI session, not from the shell. There is no hermes snapshot subcommand:

/snapshot list
/snapshot restore 20261106-194536-before-upgrade

docs.title: What a quick snapshot captures
docs.text:
Files, config, and the databases that hold state you cannot regenerate:

  • state.db, plus the per-profile stores projects.db, response_store.db, memory_store.db, verification_evidence.db
  • config.yaml, .env, auth.json
  • cron/jobs.json and cron/executions.db
  • gateway_state.json, channel_directory.json, channel_aliases.json, processes.json
  • kanban.db and kanban/boards (non-default boards; workspace attachments are skipped as regenerable)
  • Pairing stores, including platform-specific pairing JSON files

Skills, sessions, and delivered media are not part of a quick snapshot. If you need those, take a full backup.

docs.title: Full Backup
docs.text:
hermes backup writes one zip containing your configuration, skills, sessions, memory, cron definitions, and data.

# Default output: ~/hermes-backup-<timestamp>.zip
hermes backup

# Explicit path
hermes backup --output /mnt/backups/hermes-$(date +%F).zip

# Keep the newest 7 archives in the output directory instead of the default 3
hermes backup --output /mnt/backups --keep 7

# Keep everything, never prune
hermes backup --output /mnt/backups --keep 0

--keep only prunes files matching the hermes-backup-*.zip naming pattern in the output directory. It will not touch archives you named yourself, so a custom filename outside that pattern is never deleted.

docs.title: What a full backup excludes
docs.text:
Excluded Why hermes-agent and nested .git Re-clone instead node_modules, venvs, site-packages Reinstall instead __pycache__, *.pyc, *.pyo Regenerated on import .cache and tool caches Regenerable browser-profiles, browser-profile Chromium holds these locked while running, and they contain your live cookies and saved logins Prior backups/ and state-snapshots/ Otherwise each backup nests the last one checkpoints/ Session trajectory caches Model and runtime downloads Regenerable *.db-wal, *.db-shm, *.db-journal Replaced by the consistent database snapshot .backup.lock, gateway.pid, cron.pid Meaningless on another machine

Everything under cache/ is also skipped except the subdirectories that hold delivered media and generated artifacts: images, audio, videos, documents, screenshots, citations, and generated files. Those are things the agent produced for you and nothing can rebuild them.

docs.title: Restore From a Full Backup
docs.text:
# Extract into the Hermes home, prompting before overwriting
hermes import ~/hermes-backup-2026-11-06.zip

# Overwrite existing files without prompting
hermes import ~/hermes-backup-2026-11-06.zip --force

hermes import writes into the active Hermes home. Restoring onto a different machine is the intended use: install Hermes, stop the gateway, import the archive, then start the gateway again. Your skills, cron jobs, and configuration come back with the data.

docs.title: Verify a Backup Before You Trust It
docs.text:
A backup you have never opened is a guess. Two cheap checks:

# 1. The archive is readable and has the file count you expect
unzip -l ~/hermes-backup-2026-11-06.zip | tail -3

# 2. The state database inside it is a real SQLite file
unzip -p ~/hermes-backup-2026-11-06.zip state.db > /tmp/state.check.db
sqlite3 /tmp/state.check.db "PRAGMA integrity_check;"

PRAGMA integrity_check should print ok. If it prints anything else, take a new backup and investigate before relying on the old one.

docs.title: Scheduled Backups
docs.text:
A daily snapshot and a weekly archive is a reasonable default. Snapshot first, because it is cheap:

# Quick snapshot at 02:15 every day
15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/hermes backup --quick --label nightly

# Full archive every Sunday at 03:15, keep the newest 4
15 3 * * 0 /usr/local/bin/hermes backup --output /mnt/backups --keep 4

Cron runs with a minimal environment. If your Hermes install is not on the cron PATH, use the absolute path to the binary, and export HERMES_HOME in the crontab if you run more than one profile.

For off-machine durability, point --output at a mounted remote volume and let a separate tool handle versioning. The zip is a plain file, so any object storage or backup program can carry it.

docs.title: Security Warning
docs.text:
A full backup contains .env and auth.json. That means API keys, OAuth tokens, and every credential your agent uses.

  • Treat the archive as secret material, at the same level as the credentials themselves
  • Never commit it to a repository, attach it to a ticket, or upload it to a shared drive
  • Encrypt it before it leaves the machine if the destination is not under your control
  • Rotate any key that was inside an archive you lost control of

docs.title: "No such file or directory" on restore
docs.text: hermes import expects the path to the zip, and it writes relative to the active Hermes home. If you set HERMES_HOME in a different shell than the one you are restoring in, you are restoring into the wrong home. Check echo $HERMES_HOME first.

docs.title: The snapshot is listed but restoring it changes nothing
docs.text: The gateway keeps state in memory. Stop the gateway, restore, then start it again, so nothing writes the old state back over the restored files.

docs.title: A backup hangs
docs.text: A full backup takes a lock and snapshots every database. If another backup or an update is holding the slot, the second run waits. If a database is locked by a running browser session, the full backup skips the excluded profile directories but can still wait on an in-use database. Stop the process that holds it, or use --quick for the fast path.

docs.title: The archive is much smaller than expected
docs.text: Check whether your sessions and media live outside the Hermes home. A backup covers the home directory only. Anything you have symlinked elsewhere, such as a model directory or an external vault, is not in the archive and needs its own backup plan.

docs.title: Is hermes backup --quick a zip file?
docs.text: No. It creates a state snapshot directory and prints a /snapshot restore command. Use hermes backup without --quick when you need a single portable archive.

docs.title: Can I restore a quick snapshot on another machine?
docs.text: Not with hermes import, which reads zip archives. Copy the snapshot directory and the rest of the Hermes home, or take a full backup instead.

docs.title: Does the backup stop the agent?
docs.text: No. Both commands take a cross-process lock and copy databases with sqlite3.backup(), which is safe while the gateway is writing. A restore is different: stop the gateway first.

docs.title: Are my browser cookies in the backup?
docs.text: No. Live browser profile directories are excluded, because they contain a credential store and cannot be copied while Chromium holds them open.

docs.title: How many backups does Hermes keep?
docs.text: Twenty quick snapshots by default. For full archives, --keep defaults to 3 and only prunes files matching hermes-backup-*.zip; --keep 0 disables pruning.

docs.title: Cloud VPS Hermes Agent Setup - 24/7 AI Agent for $5-20/Month
docs.text: Run Hermes Agent 24/7 on a cloud VPS for always-on AI automation at minimal cost. No hardware to maintain, no electricity bill, and your agent stays online even when your laptop is off. This cloud VPS setup guide covers provisioning, model configuration, cron persistence, and security hardening.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A cloud VPS is the best budget option for always-on Hermes Agent operation. For $5-20/month you get a Linux server that runs 24/7 with built-in uptime guarantees. Use API-based models (OpenRouter for 200+ models including free-tier options) since VPS instances don't have GPUs.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Component How It Runs on Cloud VPS Models OpenRouter API (200+ models) or direct provider APIs Persistence systemd service with Restart=always Crons Hermes cron scheduler - 24/7 execution Memory Honcho + GBrain + memcore-cloud Security UFW firewall, SSH key-only auth, unattended upgrades

docs.title: Provider Comparison
docs.text:
Provider Cheapest Plan RAM CPU Best For Hetzner €4.51/mo (CX22) 4GB 2 vCPU Best value in Europe DigitalOcean $6/mo (Basic) 1GB 1 vCPU Good docs, global regions AWS Lightsail $5/mo 1GB 1 vCPU AWS ecosystem integration Vultr $6/mo 1GB 1 vCPU Many regions, hourly billing Linode $5/mo 1GB 1 vCPU Simple, reliable

Recommendation: Hetzner CX22 (4GB RAM, €4.51/mo) gives enough memory for Hermes Agent + memory stack. For lightweight cron-only usage, a 1GB droplet works.

docs.title: Step 1: Provision the VPS
docs.text:
# SSH into your VPS
ssh root@your-server-ip

# Create non-root user
adduser hermes
usermod -aG sudo hermes
su - hermes

docs.title: Step 2: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
The Hermes installer provisions its own pinned Python 3.14, Node.js, ripgrep and FFmpeg, so you only need the base utilities:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y git curl tar

docs.title: Step 3: Install Hermes Agent
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash
source ~/.bashrc
hermes profile create cloud-agent
hermes profile use cloud-agent

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Cloud Models
docs.text:
# OpenRouter - free tier models available
hermes config set OPENROUTER_API_KEY "your-key"   # written to ~/.hermes/.env
hermes model                                      # provider + default model picker

hermes model writes model.provider and model.default for you. A model id is provider-relative (qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b:free under the openrouter provider), not prefixed with the provider name. For multi-model fallback chains, edit fallback_providers in config.yaml (a YAML list that hermes config set cannot build).

See our model selection guide for tiered routing strategies.

docs.title: Step 5: Docker Option
docs.text:
For containerized deployment:

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker hermes

mkdir -p ~/.hermes
docker run -d --name hermes \
  -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data \
  -p 8642:8642 \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  nousresearch/hermes-agent gateway run

Run docker run -it --rm -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent setup once first to write your API keys into ~/.hermes/.env. Full setup in the Docker guide.

docs.title: Step 6: Systemd Service
docs.text:
The CLI can write the unit for you, which is the shorter path and keeps the paths correct:

hermes gateway install --start-now
hermes gateway status

If you want to own the unit yourself, this is the equivalent:

sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/hermes-gateway.service << 'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Hermes Agent Gateway
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=hermes
ExecStart=/home/hermes/.local/bin/hermes gateway run
Restart=always
RestartSec=10
Environment=HOME=/home/hermes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now hermes-gateway

docs.title: Step 7: Cron Persistence
docs.text:
The schedule and the prompt are positional arguments; --name and --deliver are flags:

# Email monitoring
hermes cron create "*/15 * * * *" \
  "Check inbox for unread. Summarize. Silent if empty." \
  --name email-watch

# Daily health check
hermes cron create "0 8 * * *" \
  "Verify services running. Check disk space. Report issues." \
  --name health-check

docs.title: Step 8: Security Hardening
docs.text:
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp
sudo ufw enable
ssh-copy-id hermes@your-server-ip
sudo sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config
sudo systemctl restart sshd
sudo apt install unattended-upgrades

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Always-on: 24/7 operation with cloud provider uptime guarantees
  • Budget-friendly: $5-20/month total including models
  • Zero hardware maintenance: No physical machine to manage
  • Instant scaling: Upgrade RAM/CPU with a few clicks
  • Global regions: Deploy close to your data sources
  • Free-tier models: OpenRouter offers free models for light usage

docs.title: Cost Breakdown
docs.text:
Item Monthly Cost Hetzner CX22 (4GB RAM) €4.51 OpenRouter API (free models) $0 Honcho (free tier) $0 Total ~$5/month

For heavier usage with Claude-level models: ~$15-25/month.

docs.title: Can I run local models on a cloud VPS?
docs.text: No - cloud VPS instances don't have GPUs. Use API-based models via OpenRouter or direct provider APIs. For local model inference, use a gaming PC or Mac Mini M4.

docs.title: Which cloud VPS provider is best for Hermes Agent?
docs.text: Hetzner CX22 offers the best value at €4.51/month with 4GB RAM - enough for Hermes Agent + memory stack. DigitalOcean and Linode are good alternatives with simpler interfaces.

docs.title: How do I keep Hermes Agent running after reboot?
docs.text: The systemd service with Restart=always ensures Hermes Agent restarts automatically. Combine with WantedBy=multi-user.target so it starts on boot.

docs.title: Token Refresh Guard
docs.text:
A CorpusIQ JWT access token expires after 60 minutes, so any cron that runs less often than that needs a fresh credential before it starts.

The simplest setup is to let Hermes own the token. Register the server with OAuth instead of pasting a JWT into config.yaml:

hermes mcp add corpusiq --url https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp --auth oauth
hermes mcp login corpusiq          # add --flow device for a headless host
hermes mcp test corpusiq

The server publishes OAuth 2.0 authorization-server and protected-resource metadata, so Hermes runs the flow once and keeps the credential in its own token store. Re-authenticate with hermes mcp reauth corpusiq when the 30-day refresh credential lapses.

If you keep the header-auth setup instead, refresh before the task and write the new access token into config.yaml:

curl -s -X POST https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/oauth/token \
  -d "grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=<saved_refresh_token>"

A wrapper script is the right place for that: refresh, patch headers.Authorization, then call hermes -z "<task>" in the same run.

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
• Stripe: 100 req/sec per account in live mode (25 req/sec in sandbox). Individual endpoints cap at 25 req/sec, and read calls average no more than 500 per transaction over a rolling 30 days.
  • QuickBooks Online: 500 req/min per realm (company file), 10 req/sec per realm and app, 40 batch requests per minute with up to 30 operations per batch
  • HubSpot: 100 req/10sec (burst OK, sustained <10/sec)

More patterns: corpusiq.io/docs

docs.title: How to Add CorpusIQ MCP to Hermes Agent
docs.text: Hermes Agent can use CorpusIQ as an MCP server to query business data from 40+ tools. Here's how.

docs.title: 1. Get a CorpusIQ account
docs.text: Sign up at corpusiq.io. Free trial, no credit card.

docs.title: 2. Connect your business tools
docs.text:
Go to your CorpusIQ dashboard. Connect tools via OAuth: - QuickBooks (read-only) - Stripe (read-only) - HubSpot (read-only) - Shopify (read-only) - GA4, Google Ads, Meta Ads, and 40+ more

Each takes 30 seconds. One click. No API keys to manage.

docs.title: 3. Add CorpusIQ MCP to Hermes
docs.text:
Add this to your Hermes Agent config (~/.hermes/config.yaml):

mcp_servers:
  corpusiq:
    url: "https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp"
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer <jwt>"

The Authorization header carries the JWT obtained during device authentication. Hermes picks the transport from the entry itself: url means a remote HTTP server, command plus args means a local stdio server. There is no transport key to set.

Or if using hermes mcp CLI:

hermes mcp add corpusiq --url https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp --auth header

--auth header prompts for the token and writes the Authorization header into the config entry for you.

docs.title: 4. Authenticate
docs.text:
CorpusIQ uses OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant for CLI tools and agent loops. The flow:

  1. Generate a device code: POST https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/oauth/device/authorize
  2. Open the returned verification_uri (https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/oauth/device/verify) in a browser, enter the user_code, and approve
  3. Exchange the device code for tokens: POST https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/oauth/token with form data containing ONLY grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code and device_code=<code>. Do NOT include client_id.
  4. Save both access_token (60-min expiry) and refresh_token (30-day expiry) to mcp_tokens.json
  5. Set the JWT in config: headers.Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

For the Python device login script, see the account's own token store (mcp_tokens.json) and the device flow above.

When the access token expires, refresh silently: 

curl -X POST https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/oauth/token \
  -d "grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=<saved_refresh_token>"

The refresh token flow is live in production. One device OAuth reconnect after July 28, 2026 mints the 30-day refresh credential. No hourly babysitting required.

docs.title: 5. Call tools correctly
docs.text:
All CorpusIQ MCP tool calls must nest query parameters inside the params key:

# CORRECT - params nested
await session.call_tool("search_console_connector", {
    "action": "get_performance",
    "params": {
        "site_url": "sc-domain:corpusiq.io",
        "start_date": "2026-07-01",
        "end_date": "2026-07-28",
        "dimensions": ["query"],
        "row_limit": 10
    }
})

# WRONG - flat params silently return empty or fail
await session.call_tool("search_console_connector", {
    "action": "get_performance",
    "site_url": "...",
    ...
})

The tool inputSchema defines action and params as the only two properties. All query parameters go inside params. Flat parameters alongside action will produce zero results or Tool execution failed errors.

docs.title: 6. Ask questions
docs.text:
Now your Hermes Agent can answer business questions from live data:

"What's our revenue this month vs last month across Stripe and QuickBooks?"

"Show me HubSpot pipeline by stage. Which deals are stuck?"

"What's our blended ROAS across Google Ads and Meta Ads this week?"

docs.title: Tools available
docs.text: CorpusIQ exposes 40+ connectors as MCP tools. Hermes auto-discovers them. No code. No SDK. Just connect and ask.

docs.title: Operation-level safety
docs.text: External-source retrieval tools are marked read-only. Write-capable connector-management and CorpusIQ control-plane tools are separately named and annotated; provider scopes vary by connector. Direct MCP does not retain raw customer files or full connector response payloads; scoped operational logs may persist for up to 30 days.

docs.title: Token refresh for crons
docs.text:
The refresh token (30-day expiry) is now available in production. Save both access_token and refresh_token from the device OAuth response. When the access token expires, POST grant_type=refresh_token to /oauth/token for a new one. Never overwrite the refresh token when updating the access token.

For cron jobs, wrap the task so the token is refreshed before the run, then call the one-shot mode:

# 1. refresh (returns a new access_token; keep the refresh_token unchanged)
curl -s -X POST https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/oauth/token \
  -d "grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=<saved_refresh_token>"

# 2. write the returned access_token into headers.Authorization in config.yaml

# 3. run the task
hermes -z "your task"

Your wrapper script owns steps 1 and 2; the agent only ever sees a valid JWT.

Complete docs: github.com/CorpusIQ/corpusiq-docs

docs.title: Docker Hermes Agent Setup - Reproducible Container Deployment
docs.text: Deploy Hermes Agent as a Docker container for identical behavior on your laptop, a cloud VPS, or a CI/CD pipeline. No Python version conflicts, no dependency hell - just consistent, reproducible AI agent deployment. This Docker setup guide covers Compose configuration, volume management, MCP integration, and production hardening.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Docker deployment is the most portable way to run Hermes Agent. The official nousresearch/hermes-agent image ships with all dependencies pre-installed (Python 3.14, Node.js, Chromium). Mount your data directory as a volume for persistence, set API keys as environment variables, and you're running in under 2 minutes.

The image is stateless: every piece of mutable state lives in the single data directory mounted from the host at /opt/data. The installed application tree at /opt/hermes is root-owned and read-only to the runtime user, so a plain image pull upgrades the agent without touching your config.

Image tag Meaning latest / stable Accepted by the stable release gate main Development image built from the main branch X.Y.Z Versioned stable image; pin a digest for exact deployments

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: Component Docker Approach Hermes binary Pre-installed at /opt/hermes in the container image Configuration Host directory mounted at /opt/data (~/.hermes by default) API keys /opt/data/.env inside the container, or environment variables Skills Under /opt/data/skills in the mounted volume Crons Stored in the volume, survive restarts MCP servers Run inside container, added via docker compose exec

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Run the setup wizard once to write your keys to ~/.hermes/.env:

mkdir -p ~/.hermes
docker run -it --rm \
  -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data \
  nousresearch/hermes-agent setup

For unattended operation, hermes setup --portal inside the container is the lowest-friction path: the refresh token persists in the mounted volume, so nothing expires while you are not watching.

Then start the container as a persistent gateway:

docker run -d --name hermes \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data \
  -p 8642:8642 \
  nousresearch/hermes-agent gateway run

Port 8642 exposes the gateway's OpenAI-compatible API server and health endpoint. It is optional if you only use chat platforms, and required if you want the dashboard or external tools to reach the gateway. Inside the official image the gateway is supervised by s6-overlay, so a crash restarts it in seconds without losing the container.

Three container details worth knowing before you copy the Compose file:

  • The API server is gated on API_SERVER_ENABLED=true. To reach it beyond 127.0.0.1, also set API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0 and an API_SERVER_KEY of at least 8 characters (openssl rand -hex 32).
  • The dashboard on 9119 fails closed. A non-loopback bind refuses to start unless a dashboard auth provider is configured (username/password via HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME + _PASSWORD, Nous Portal OAuth, or self-hosted OIDC), and HERMES_DASHBOARD_INSECURE is now a deprecated no-op. The Compose file below keeps that port on 127.0.0.1, so it is reachable only through an SSH tunnel until you add a provider.
  • Browser tools need shared memory. Chromium in a container wants --shm-size=1g (shm_size: 1g in Compose). If the browser is missing, install it inside the container with hermes pm install chromium; browser.executable_path in the mounted config.yaml overrides the packaged build.

docs.title: Full docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
services:
  hermes:
    image: nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest
    container_name: hermes
    restart: unless-stopped

    command: ["gateway", "run"]

    volumes:
      # All mutable state lives here: config, .env, skills, sessions, crons.
      - ~/.hermes:/opt/data

    environment:
      # Keep files created in the container owned by your host user.
      - HERMES_UID=${HERMES_UID:-10000}
      - HERMES_GID=${HERMES_GID:-10000}
      - TZ=${TZ:-UTC}

    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8642:8642"   # OpenAI-compatible API server (optional)
      - "127.0.0.1:9119:9119"   # dashboard (only with HERMES_DASHBOARD=1)

    healthcheck:
      # Liveness only. `hermes doctor` exits non-zero on advisories such as
      # npm vulnerability notices, so it would mark a working container
      # unhealthy. Use it interactively, not as a healthcheck.
      test: ["CMD", "hermes", "--version"]
      interval: 60s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

The top-level version: key is obsolete in Compose v2 and is omitted here; Docker Compose warns about it and ignores the value.

docs.title: Launch
docs.text:
mkdir -p ~/.hermes
export HERMES_UID=$(id -u) HERMES_GID=$(id -g)
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f hermes
docker compose exec hermes hermes doctor

The model is a config value, not an environment variable. Set it inside the container:

docker compose exec hermes hermes model          # interactive picker
docker compose exec hermes hermes config set model.default "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6"

docs.title: Adding MCP Servers
docs.text:
# Remote HTTP/SSE server
docker compose exec hermes hermes mcp add corpusiq --url https://mcp2.corpusiq.io/mcp

# Remote server that needs a bearer token (prompts for the key, saves it to /opt/data/.env)
docker compose exec hermes hermes mcp add honcho --url https://mcp.honcho.dev --auth header

# GitHub's official remote server (the @modelcontextprotocol/server-github npm
# package is archived and unmaintained); --auth header prompts for the token
docker compose exec hermes hermes mcp add github --url https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --auth header

# Stdio server: --args must be the last option
docker compose exec hermes hermes mcp add filesystem --command npx --args -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /opt/data

Verify with docker compose exec hermes hermes mcp test corpusiq. See the MCP Integration Guide for all available servers.

docs.title: Crons and Persistence
docs.text:
The schedule and the prompt are positional arguments; --name and --deliver are flags:

docker compose exec hermes hermes cron create "*/15 * * * *" \
  "Check inbox. Summarize unread." \
  --name email-watch \
  --deliver local

Crons survive container restarts and image updates because they're stored under /opt/data in the mounted volume. Follow cron design best practices for production-grade scheduling.

docs.title: Production Checklist
docs.text:
# 1. Resource limits
# Add to docker-compose.yml:
#   deploy:
#     resources:
#       limits:
#         memory: 2G
#         cpus: "2"

# 2. Log rotation
#   logging:
#     driver: "json-file"
#     options:
#       max-size: "10m"
#       max-file: "3"

# 3. Monitor health
docker compose ps
docker compose exec hermes hermes gateway status

docs.title: Docker on Different Hosts
docs.text: Host Notes Local laptop Development and testing Cloud VPS Add --restart unless-stopped for 24/7 NAS / home server Mount large volumes for GBrain embeddings CI/CD Ephemeral volumes for automated testing

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Reproducible: Identical behavior everywhere
  • No dependency conflicts: Everything bundled in container
  • Portable: Same Compose file works on laptop, VPS, or CI/CD
  • Persistent: The mounted data directory survives updates and restarts
  • Production-ready: Health checks, restart policies, log rotation built in

docs.title: Do I need to rebuild the Docker image for updates?
docs.text: No - docker compose pull fetches the latest image from Docker Hub. Your config, skills, and crons persist in the mounted volume.

docs.title: Can I run GPU-accelerated models in Docker?
docs.text: Yes, if the host has an NVIDIA GPU and the NVIDIA Container Toolkit installed. Pass --gpus all to docker run or add deploy.resources.reservations.devices in Compose.

docs.title: How do I add custom skills to Docker Hermes?
docs.text: Put them in the mounted data directory: ~/.hermes/skills/ on the host is /opt/data/skills in the container. No extra mount is needed, and new skills are picked up on the next session. See the custom skills guide.
